Day and night they practice, transcending the eight difficulties; their physical forms are dignified and majestic, all appearing as one.
Seven layers of rows of trees and seven layers of railings; Jeweled canopies hang in the sky, draped with jeweled nets.
All who possess the karmic affinity may behold them; Those who study with earnest devotion contemplate them with focused minds.
When people arrive, they ride upon flowers and sit within the jeweled groves; The devas come to play music, its melodies profound and deep.
The Six Perfections have already harmonized the six musical scales; The Eightfold Path further blends the eight tones.
In the jewel-pool of virtue, the water is clear and the sand beneath is fresh; Lotuses bloom with radiance like chariot wheels.
The Bodhisattva sits upright upon a flower; All who gaze upon him are destined for rebirth there.
In the Dharma-king’s realm of Amitābha’s Pure Land, The adornments of his vows sprout the teeth of the Way.
Within the jade-green pavilion, precious thrones fly; Upon the golden ground, heavenly flowers rain down.
Having gathered the celestial flower robes in his lap, His six supernormal powers are at will and his enlightened body is light.
Having made offerings to the Buddhas of the other directions, they return to their own lands to provide food for the walking monks;
the birds sing in harmony throughout the six periods of the day, their pure sounds expounding the Dharma in a wondrous and inconceivable manner.
The five faculties of the five directions and the seven factors of enlightenment, along with the profound eightfold noble path, lead one into the unconditioned state.
The assembly simultaneously listens to the sound of the Dharma; All who hear it give rise to the mind that recollects the Buddha.
The transformed birds were originally not of the three evil realms;
As Amitābha proclaims the profound and subtle flow of the Dharma, A pure breeze stirs the jewel forest, And its resonant echoes soar like the music played by celestial beings.
In each and every place, no other distinct teaching is proclaimed; everywhere one hears only the name of the Buddha of Recollection.
The lifespan of Amitābha is truly boundless, and so too are the people within his land.
He attained the Way ten kalpas ago, and his light illuminates the Dharma-realm as vast as the sands of the Ganges.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas is vast; those seeking liberation who behold Amitābha cannot calculate its limits even by number. Buddhas from other directions also come there;
it is heard that the Pure Land is exceedingly sublime and true, filled entirely with those who are non-retrogressive (avaivartika).
Those in their final birth who cultivate samādhi attain the adamantine final body;
With meager roots of goodness and little merit, such a state is difficult to produce by principle.
If one focuses exclusively on reciting the Buddha’s name for seven days, And remains undisturbed in mind at the time of death, Amitābha will surely come to welcome them personally.
The Ten Epithets of Amitābha repay past causes; The Buddhas of the six directions testify that he has realized the truth.
His tongue is broad and long, for he speaks no falsehoods; The Tathāgata protects and mindful of those with faith.
The world is impermanent and cannot be stayed long; One must simply resolve to seek it diligently and early.
Those already born and those yet to be born shall all never fall back; how could there be any distinction between those who have practiced now and those who have not?

All Buddhas simultaneously praise Śākyamuni, who is able to save the Sahā world amidst the five turbidities by preaching this Dharma that is difficult for the world to believe, causing all to awaken and keep Amitābha in mind.
The Dharma-treasury has fully expounded the meaning; from this point, Ānanda shall propagate the true exposition.
The great assembly all rejoice and receive it upon their heads.
The Buddha-lands and pure realms appear according to the mind—how inconceivable! All manner of adornments arise within the mind—how inconceivable! Vimalakīrti.
Pressing the earth with his toes, the three thousandfold world-system is inconceivable; sitting upon a flower pedestal within the ocean-like nature of space, it is inconceivable.
The chamber of ten feet square in the city of Vaiśālī is inconceivable;
there is a layman named Vimalakīrti who manifests illness through a pretext of sickness, which is inconceivable. That the ruler of the land and the princes all come to visit him is inconceivable.

The immeasurable assembly of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas is inconceivable; none among them can bear to be sent to inquire after his illness, except for Mañjuśrī, who dares to enter and question this inconceivable one. "What is the cause of the householder’s illness? he asked.
"It is inconceivable," Vimalakīrti replied, "the illness arises from ignorance and craving. "My illness is neither existent nor non-existent; it is inconceivable, Mañjuśrī."

To explain in detail: that the body is an impermanent dharma is inconceivable; that the body is a composite of the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*) is inconceivable.
That the tip of a bodhisattva’s hair can contain a great ocean is inconceivable; that Mount Sumeru is contained within a mustard seed is inconceivable.
That Vimalakīrti cast a world into another realm with his hand is inconceivable; that the goddesses in his room realized non-arising (*anutpāda*) is inconceivable.
In the Śāla Grove, within the twin trees, when the Buddha entered nirvāṇa, tears fell like clouds and rain;
they fell in torrents, spontaneously shattering his golden couch. Tears fell like clouds and rain; the crown and robes of the seven jewels spontaneously shattered.
Within the twin trees, blood flowed from his seven orifices, forming a pool; tears fell like clouds and rain. A celestial maiden brought water to sprinkle upon his face within the twin trees.

After a long while, the Mother of Buddhas regained her senses; tears fell like clouds and rain as she descended upon the Twin Śāla Grove with a host of celestial maidens, arriving directly amidst the twin *śāla* trees where her tears fell like clouds and rain.

Once the enshrinement within the golden coffin and silver casket was completed inside the Twin Grove, the monastic robes and mendicant’s staff hung suspended among the trees as her tears fell like clouds and rain.
The ten great disciples wailed and wept aloud within the Twin Grove.

Resembling an infant yearning for its mother, tears fall like clouds and rain; The Mother of Buddhas circumambulates the coffin, wailing piteously within the Twin Trees, as a hundred birds gather to share her grief, their tears falling like clouds and rain.
Others say that parting while alive is worse than parting in death;

Within the Twin Trees, I say that parting in death is better than parting while alive, as tears fall like clouds and rain. The golden coffin and silver outer casing suddenly open within the Twin Trees.

Sitting upon a thousand-petaled lotus pedestal, tears fall like clouds and rain. Within the flowers, the Tathāgata speaks for his mother: "In the grove of the twin śāla trees, all affectionate bonds are subject to separation; tears fall like clouds and rain.
Though one is briefly parted from a compassionate parent for a small kalpa, within the grove of the twin śāla trees there is the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi.
I vow to be reborn there; by single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha, one shall behold Amitābha and experience immeasurable bliss."
I universally exhort you to turn your minds and aspire to be born in the Pure Land; by turning your minds to recite the Buddha’s name, you shall be reborn together in immeasurable bliss.
For immeasurable eons we have wandered long through the realms of existence; I pray that you will aspire to be born there. Following conditions, we undergo the cycle of rebirth within the six paths;

I pray that you will aspire to be born there. If you do not meet a spiritual friend who can urge you toward rebirth, how could you attain immeasurable bliss? I pray that you will aspire to be born there. Who can exhort you to return [to the source] and attain immeasurable bliss? I pray that you will aspire to be born there.

Recalling the fleeting pleasures of the celestial realms, I vow to be reborn there; yet when merit is exhausted and death approaches, the five signs of decay appear—recalling the immeasurable suffering of being conceived in a human womb, I vow to be reborn there;
where four snakes and six thieves compete to hasten one’s end, amidst immeasurable suffering.
Recalling the immeasurable suffering of the asura and preta realms, where hunger, emptiness, and strife are difficult to quell, I vow to be reborn there; amidst immeasurable suffering.

Recalling the suffering of being devoured by one another among the animals, may I vow to be reborn there; Recalling the immeasurable joy of casting off life amidst the glare of blades, yet still being led away to further sufferings, may I vow to be reborn there;
Recalling the immeasurable joy of the long-lasting sufferings of the hells, where one is blown away by the winds of karma and knows no turning back, may I vow to be reborn there;
Recalling the immeasurable joy of ascending the mountain of blades or climbing the tree of swords, where skin, flesh, and bones turn to ash, may I vow to be reborn there.
Some enter boiling cauldrons and fiery furnaces, praying for rebirth in the Land of Infinite Bliss; amidst surging waves and fierce flames more violent than thunder, they ask:
by what cause do they receive such suffering while seeking Infinite Bliss? Clinging to fish and craving meat, their karma follows them;

they must drink molten copper poured into their mouths and have their tongues plowed like fields—praying for rebirth in the Land of Infinite Bliss. Having drunk wine and spoken falsehoods, they now suffer this calamity—praying for rebirth in the Land of Infinite Bliss.
Or lying upon iron beds and embracing copper pillars, may they vow to be reborn there—endless bliss for those who, through perverse lust, have come [to this state].
Or falling into the great Avīci Hell, may they vow to be reborn there—endless bliss for those whose eyes remain unopened throughout kalpas of long years.
Or passing through the intermingling of upper and lower fires, may they vow to be reborn there—endless bliss for those upon whom blades, wheels, and iron pestles fly down from above.
May those whose hearts are bitten by copper dogs and whose blood is devoured, and those whose eyes are pecked out by iron crows and whose cheeks are pierced, aspire to be born there.

May the assembly at this present site of enlightenment aspire to be born there, where immeasurable bliss prevails. Having passed through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, immeasurable bliss is attained;

since it is difficult for a human body to encounter such a state, may all aspire to be born there. It is like the first blooming of the Udumbara flower—immeasurable bliss! May all aspire to be born there.
Precisely at this time, the rarely heard teaching of the Pure Land opens the vow for rebirth; Precisely at this time, the Dharma-gate of Buddha-remembrance unfolds immeasurable bliss.
Precisely at this time, Amitābha’s great vows call forth the vow for rebirth; Precisely at this time, the great assembly turns their faith toward immeasurable bliss.
Precisely at this time, according to the sutras, we praise the vow for rebirth; Precisely at this time, we bind our covenant upon the flower pedestal of immeasurable bliss.
Precisely when the Way-place is free from demonic hindrances, I vow to be born there; Precisely when one is free from illness and can come in full strength, it is a time of immeasurable joy.
Precisely when the merit of one day or seven days is accomplished, I vow to be born there; The essential aim of the forty-eight vows is to lead us together in immeasurable joy.
I universally exhort all fellow practitioners at the Way-place to vow to be born there; Exert yourselves, turn your minds, and return! It is a time of immeasurable joy.
I ask, where is your native land? I vow to be reborn upon the seven-jeweled terraces within the pond of Ultimate Bliss; there is immeasurable joy.

Having established great vows while practicing the causes for that Buddha, I vow to welcome all who hear my name and remember me; there is immeasurable joy. I do not discriminate between the poor and the wealthy;
I vow to welcome them all; there is immeasurable joy. I do not discriminate between the lowly and the high, or the ignorant and the talented; there is immeasurable joy.
Without distinction for those who lack the karma or vows for the Pure Land, they vow to be born there; Without distinction for non-Buddhists or icchantikas, they vow to enjoy immeasurable bliss;
Without distinction for those who have only today begun to give rise to the mind of awakening, they vow to enjoy immeasurable bliss;

Without distinction for those of many learnings or who uphold pure precepts, they vow to be born there; Without distinction for those who have broken the precepts or whose roots of sin are deep, they vow to enjoy immeasurable bliss.
Simply turn your minds toward the Buddha, recite his name, and vow to be born in the Pure Land; this can transform rubble into gold—this is immeasurable bliss.
I entrust this to the great assembly gathered here: vow to be born in the Pure Land. Those who share this same aspiration, go quickly to seek one another—this is immeasurable bliss.
I ask where you go to seek one another: report that it is within the Pure Land of Amitābha—this is immeasurable bliss.
I ask: by what cause can one be born there? I vow to be reborn there. The answer: through the practice of *nien-fo*, success is spontaneously achieved;
it is immeasurable bliss. I ask: those who have committed many karmic obstacles in this life, how can the Pure Land be willing to admit them?
The answer: by reciting the Name, sins are extinguished; I vow to be reborn there. It is like a bright lamp entering the darkness; it is immeasurable bliss.
I ask: do ordinary beings attain birth [in the Pure Land]? They do not wish for rebirth there. How can a single thought bring light to the darkness? The answer:
eliminate doubt, focus exclusively on the Buddha’s name, and vow for rebirth. At the moment of death, the precious throne will surely come to welcome you.

The Great Assembly, everyone with palms joined, proclaims the joy of the Dharma-assembly. With bodies broken in prostration, they express their gratitude for Śākyamuni’s kindness. The joy of the Dharma-assembly!

The joy of the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) is the attainment of the path of skillful means through compassion; The joy of the site of enlightenment is the instruction on the gate of happiness in the Western Land.

When the assembly at the site of enlightenment is about to disperse and those who have gathered are about to part, One should exert effort and exhort one another to sever greed and anger—the joy of the site of enlightenment.
Greed and anger are the causes and conditions that obstruct the Pure Land; Without attaining liberation, one will sink forever into the depths—this is the joy of the site of enlightenment.

The joy of the practice hall, where companions walk together, support one another, and exhort each other; The joy of the practice hall, vowing to reach the presence of the Buddha even at the end of life;
The joy of the practice hall, may this wheel of Dharma turn in continuous succession; The joy of the practice hall, may the assembly of the practice hall increase in years;
The joy of the practice hall, may we all together receive this happiness; The joy of the practice hall, those who see, hear, or rejoice in it shall likewise do so.
May the assembly turn their minds toward the joy of the Pure Land’s place of practice; Holding incense and flowers, they proceed to the place of practice in the West.
Lofty is Amitābha, his countenance of purple-gold brilliance; His physical marks are the thirty-two, with level soles beneath his feet;
He possesses the eighty secondary signs, his radiance constantly illuminating all.
The Brahma-voice transcends the three thousandfold world; its wondrous resonance is like the cry of the mournful pheasant.
Lofty and majestic is the land of Amitābha, exceedingly pure and bright, entirely of golden hue. There are no names for the four evil women;
the waters of the ponds flow into one another. The jeweled trees produce the five musical notes, singing praises of impermanence and suffering.
Upon hearing this, all attain non-arising; Sublime is Amitābha, the King of All Virtues.
His land is wondrously peaceful and blissful; there is none who does not wish to be reborn there.
The Buddha and the assembly of Bodhisattvas fly forth together to welcome them; suddenly, within the ponds of the seven treasures, they grow to maturity amidst the lotus flowers.
Lofty is Amitābha, His majestic virtue wondrous and peerless; His body is of true golden hue, Radiating light throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Whoever hears of him, beholds him, or encounters him, Shall forever uproot the suffering of birth and death.
I now prostrate in homage To the Unsurpassed Father of Beings. Having finished reciting this praise.
One should immediately recite the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva twenty-one times.
When sentient beings are beset by calamities, And their bodies are oppressed by immeasurable suffering,
The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can rescue them from the world’s pains, Even when involved in litigation before the authorities or amidst the terrors of battle.
By recollecting the power of that Avalokiteśvara, all enemies shall completely retreat and disperse.
With wondrous voice, voice of the world-observer, Brahma-voice, and ocean-tide voice— surpassing all sounds in this world— therefore one must constantly maintain mindfulness;
do not give rise to doubt. Avalokiteśvara, the pure and holy one, [is the refuge] amidst suffering, affliction, and the peril of death.
Able to act as a refuge, Possessing all virtuous qualities, Beholding sentient beings with eyes of compassion, An ocean of merit immeasurable— Therefore, one should pay homage.
Upon finishing this praise, one should then recite the name of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva twenty-one times.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva possesses sovereign supernormal powers that are equal to those of Avalokiteśvara, without any difference.
The two Great Beings, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Constantly attend upon Amitābha Buddha at His left and right.
Avalokiteśvara wears Amitābha Buddha upon his crown;
Within Mahāsthāmaprāpta’s crown is a precious vase, From within which radiates light of immeasurable extent, Constantly emitting brilliance that illuminates suffering sentient beings.
With compassion, joy, and equanimity, one constantly engages with sentient beings; whatever one undertakes is never in vain.
The joy of leaving the household life! The joy of leaving the household life!

Arising from the beginningless past, one delights in all attachments, yet now, meeting with the virtuous, cuts through kinship ties. Suddenly casting off worldly sentiments, one severs all evils; severing all evils.
Arousing body and mind, relying on the noble training, one eliminates the fetters and afflictions.

With the golden blade falling, hair is shorn and the robes are donned; one partakes of the precious medicine, nourished by the precious medicine. Cherishing the joy of the Dharma, one leaps with exultation.
Who could remain in the long night of heavy darkness? On this day, purifying the body, one rejoices in Great Awakening—rejoicing in Great Awakening!
The Joy of Leaving Home The joy of leaving home transcends all worldly affairs.
Having reached the age of twenty, I met a preceptor; Respectfully receiving the *śīla*, I encountered a pure ordination platform.
Upon encountering this pure platform, I cultivated concentration and wisdom; Realization was not difficult to attain. Awakening is as clear as lapis lazuli, illuminating both within and without.
Exquisite like a lotus flower, behold it freely; behold all things freely. Honored as a son of the Dharma, the gateway of the teaching is vast.
Entering and exiting, going and coming, there is no obstruction on the path. Liberated and carefree, one realizes nirvana;
realizing nirvana, go back and come forth. The precious gate opens; with right view, Amitābha ascends the jeweled throne.
The Bodhisattvas scatter flowers, crying out "Excellent! Excellent! In the Jewel Forest, the hundred-flowered fragrant waters, birds, and trees chant the Fivefold Assembly.
With plaintive and compassionate voices, they praise the Dharma King;
The *saṃjīva* birds face the mandarin ducks, And the parrots and *kalaviṅka* birds proclaim the wondrous Dharma.
Return! Return! Depart from Sahā; Always remain with the Tathāgata to hear the wondrous Dharma.
Return! Return! Behold Amitābha; He now appears in the West preaching the Dharma.
Return! Return! Ascend the golden terrace; Śrīmati and Avalokiteśvara come to lead the way.
The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land! The Pure Land is inconceivable. The joy of the Pure Land:
Amitābha dwells within a precious jeweled tower. The joy of the Pure Land: With every thought and every moment, incline your heart toward the West. The joy of the Pure Land:

Upon reaching that place, one attains the three insights and the eight liberations. The joy of the Pure Land: Forever parting from this turbid world, what more could there be to worry about? The joy of the Pure Land!
The bliss of the Pure Land! The bliss of the Pure Land! The inconceivable bliss of the Pure Land!

The bliss of the Pure Land, with jeweled towers, jeweled pavilions, and jeweled canopies held aloft! The bliss of the Pure Land, where the pond waters reflect golden sands at their bottom in pure clarity!

The bliss of the Pure Land, where the Dharma melodies are constantly offered at all times! The bliss of the Pure Land, where within the Lotus Assembly, the state of non-arising is expounded! The bliss of the Pure Land!
The bliss of the Pure Land! The bliss of the Pure Land! The inconceivable bliss of the Pure Land! The bliss of the Pure Land!
Jeweled terraces, jeweled pavilions, and precious pearls—the bliss of the Pure Land! Jeweled forms, dignified and majestic, with golden bodies—the bliss of the Pure Land!
Bodhisattvas born by transformation play upon jade strings—the bliss of the Pure Land! Gentle breezes in five harmonies expound the True Suchness—the bliss of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Pure Land is inconceivable. The joy of the Pure Land!
Flowing waters and ripples surround the jeweled terraces; The joy of the Pure Land! Radiant jewel palaces open their jade doors.
The joy of the Pure Land! The Compassionate Lord hears the sons of the three realms from afar; The joy of the Pure Land! All must resolve to be reborn there. The joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful. The joy of the Pure Land!
The body of Amitābha is vast and boundless. The joy of the Pure Land! His face resembles refined gold and the *utpala* flower. The joy of the Pure Land! His eyes are like blue lotuses.

The joy of the Pure Land! The four great oceans are [but a drop compared to it]. The joy of the Pure Land! The transformed Buddhas within his halo are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful;
the joy of the Pure Land is the Great Compassion of Amitābha’s Original Vow. The people of this world do not perceive the joy of the Pure Land;

the joy of the Pure Land is the welcoming reception as the nine grades of lotuses bloom. The joy of the Pure Land—fearing that sentient beings might emerge from the world too late. The joy of the Pure Land!
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is most exceedingly blissful.
Joyful is the Pure Land where Maitreya’s spring trees and awakening flowers bloom; Sitting upon a jeweled terrace within the pond of merit, there is joy in the Pure Land.
Before the pavilion of samādhi, one seeks liberation; there is joy in the Pure Land. In the Maṇi Hall, one pays homage to the Tathāgata; there is joy in the Pure Land.
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is exceedingly blissful.
Joyful is the Pure Land, where exotic birds are beyond counting; Joyful is the Pure Land, with white cranes, peacocks, and *kalaviṅkas*.
Joyful is the Pure Land, where parrots and *śārikas* proclaim the wondrous Dharma; From their voices, the principles of the Mahāyāna are brought forth—joyful is the Pure Land!
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is most exceedingly blissful.
In the Pure Land, the Honored Name of the Tathāgata is most clearly manifest; Joyful is the Pure Land, spreading throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Joyful is the Pure Land: whoever merely utters His name shall go there; Joyful is the Pure Land: Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta come in person to welcome them. Joyful is the Pure Land!
Joyful is the Pure Land! Joyful is the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is exceedingly joyful.
Joyful is the Pure Land where Amitābha’s followers possess universal compassion; Joyful is the Pure Land where their intent to pity sentient beings is profound.
Joyful is the Pure Land where the water-birds and forest trees preach the wondrous Dharma; How much more so the Tathāgata’s own subtle and wondrous voice! Joyful is the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful.
The joy of the Pure Land is uniquely transcendent through the Tathāgata’s original vow. Through compassion and skillful means, it leads the ordinary and the ignorant.
The joy of the Pure Land: all sentient beings, without exception, are delivered. The joy of the Pure Land: by invoking the Name, transgressions are immediately eliminated. The joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful;
In the Pure Land, Amitābha sits serenely within a precious golden pavilion. The joy of the Pure Land! Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges roam on all sides through the Pure Land.

The joy of the Pure Land! All nine classes of beings receive his light and hear him preach the wondrous Dharma. The joy of the Pure Land! Those who hear it awaken to understanding and shall forever be free from sorrow. The joy of the Pure Land!
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is exceedingly blissful.
Joyful is the Pure Land, the Western Pure Land is free from the clamor and dust of the world. When sentient beings arrive there, they immediately sever greed and anger;

joyful is the Pure Land. It is entirely composed of virtuous people and bodhisattvas; joyful is the Pure Land. Furthermore, there are no evil realms, nor any distinction between enemies and kin; joyful is the Pure Land.
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is exceedingly blissful.
Joyful is the Pure Land, where flower-banners hang on eight sides with golden bells; Joyful is the Pure Land, where harmonious sounds from above and below produce wondrous voices.
Joyful is the Pure Land, for all who hear it say it is called happiness; Joyful is the Pure Land, where for long eons the names of various sufferings are not heard. Joyful is the Pure Land!
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is exceedingly blissful. Joyful is the Pure Land;
if ordinary beings reach the Western Pure Land, Sins accumulated over kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shall perish.

Joyful is the Pure Land; endowed with the six supernatural powers, one attains mastery. Joyful is the Pure Land; forever free from old age and illness, one transcends impermanence. Joyful is the Pure Land.
Joyful is the Pure Land, joyful is the Pure Land; The Western Pure Land is most blissful.
Joyful is the Pure Land, the Western Pure Land where one is free from the womb; When sentient beings arrive, they immediately emerge from the lotus pedestal.

Joyful is the Pure Land; those of the highest grade seek the light and ascend the jeweled throne. Joyful is the Pure Land; those of the lower grades have their obstructions exhausted before the flower finally opens. Joyful is the Pure Land.
Joyful is the Pure Land! Joyful is the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is exceedingly joyful. Joyful is the Pure Land; the Western Pure Land has sevenfold railings.
Joyful is the Pure Land, adorned with hundreds of varieties of the seven treasures.

Joyful is the Pure Land, where the ground is made of lapis lazuli and is golden in color. Joyful is the Pure Land, where the various terraces and pavilions reach toward the heavens. Joyful is the Pure Land! Joyful is the Pure Land!
Joy of the Pure Land! Joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful. Joy of the Pure Land!
The Western Pure Land is rare throughout the ten directions. Joy of the Pure Land! Strive with single-mindedness and do not harbor doubt.

Joy of the Pure Land! Those of the highest grade immediately realize the patience of non-arising. Joy of the Pure Land! Those of the lower grades have their obstructions exhausted and emerge from the mire of suffering. Joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land! The Western Pure Land is most blissful; The joy of the Pure Land!

In the Western Pure Land there is nothing that surpasses it. In Jambudvīpa, those who commit sins suffer extreme misery; If one desires to escape the triple world in this very life, one must seek the joy of the Pure Land.
To attain the joy of the Pure Land, one need only focus the mind single-mindedly on Amitābha. The joy of the Pure Land! The joy of the Pure Land!
The joy of the Pure Land, the joy of the Pure Land! In the Western Pure Land there is supreme bliss. The joy of the Pure Land, I rejoice in the purity;
the joy of the Pure Land, I rejoice in the purity! Illuminating the emptiness of the mind, one realizes the world.
I rejoice in the purity of the eye-faculty, which is ever pure; I rejoice in the purity! The realm of form is originally and fundamentally empty; I rejoice in the purity!
The nature of form is originally unobstructed—this is my pure joy; Without coming and without going, this is the True Teaching—this is my pure joy.
I observe that the faculty of hearing is ever-pure—this is my pure joy; The realm of sound is fundamentally and originally empty—this is my pure joy.
The nature of sound is originally unobstructed—this is my pure joy; Without coming and without going, this is the True Teaching—this is my pure joy.
Contemplating that the nose-faculty is eternally pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The realm of fragrance is fundamentally empty from the beginning— I am pure, blissful, and joyful.
The nature of fragrance is originally without obstruction— I am pure, blissful, and joyful; Coming from nowhere and going nowhere is the True Teaching— I am pure, blissful, and joyful.
Contemplating that the tongue-faculty is eternally pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The realm of flavor is fundamentally empty from the beginning— I am pure, blissful, and joyful.
The nature of taste is originally unobstructed; my purity and bliss— Neither coming nor going is the True宗 (Teaching);
my purity and bliss. I observe that the faculty of the body is ever pure; my purity and bliss— The realm of form has always been fundamentally empty;
my purity and bliss. The nature of form is originally unobstructed; my purity and bliss— Neither coming nor going is the True宗 (Teaching); my purity and bliss.
Observing that the faculty of mind is ever-pure, I am pure, blissful, and joyful; The Dharma-realm is originally and fundamentally empty, I am pure, blissful, and joyful.

One must accomplish the merit of the Pure Land for seven days, With every thought and inclination of the heart directed toward that land. In a single *kṣaṇa*, one shall then sit within a lotus palace.
The power of Amitābha’s vows is inconceivable; The adornment of his Pure Land is most rare and wondrous.
The Buddhas of the six directions praise him simultaneously, Intending to cause all disciples to sever their doubts.
Human life is impermanent like a fleeting instant; For eternal kalpas, many have sunk into the evil realms.
One must quickly and single-mindedly recollect that Buddha; together with you, we shall cross the river of craving.
All Buddhas with one heart praise Śākyamuni, who is able to deliver many people from the sea of suffering.
He causes each and every one to focus exclusively on the Buddha-remembrance, so that in birth after birth they may always behold Amitābha.
After the Tathāgata had finished speaking, Ānanda proclaimed: "May all sentient beings who possess the karmic affinity be transformed;
All must receive this with hearts full of reverence and uphold it upon their heads. Spread far and wide this pure teaching so that it may circulate extensively.
In the past, there was a rishi named Shanhui (Good Wisdom) Who once purchased five stalks of flowers."
Taking these to offer to Dīpaṃkara Buddha, He was named Śākyamuni because of the flowers and fruit;
All the sūtras speak of wondrous gāthās, Scattering flowers as offerings to the Field of Merit.
By scattering even a single flower before a single Buddha, One shall, by virtue of that flower, attain the vision of Amitābha.
Nowadays, when the wise see the scriptural passage where the Buddha declares that flowers are the cause for attaining Buddhahood, they immediately scatter flowers as an offering to the Buddha;
furthermore, they use these flowers to deliver those with whom they have a karmic connection.
Amidst this profusion of right view, as the flowers are scattered, each petal flies through the void, moving in a verdant swirl.
Each vies to reach forward and grasp it with their hands; Everyone gathers it in their robes and returns home.
In the sky, piece after piece rains down like celestial flowers; Scattered upon everyone, they cause the sprouts of the Way to grow.
If one but makes diligent offerings of these flowers, The field of merit will extend throughout as many worlds as there are sands in the Ganges.
Flowers fly whirling through the entirety of space; Green leaves flutter, filling the realms.
With a rustling sound like horses, they descend with the clouds; In profusion, they escort the Son into the Lotus Palace.
The lotus flowers are lush and exceedingly vast and level; Upon the flowers, throngs of Bodhisattvas walk.
From time to time they scatter flowers as offerings to the Buddha; Everywhere they proclaim the sounds of the five assemblies.
The robes of all the various holy multitudes are filled with flowers; Every person makes offerings throughout lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
At every mealtime they return to their own lands; In every step they never depart from the World-Honored One’s home.
From time to time, the heavens rain down myriad flowers; Everywhere they are able to sprout the seeds of the Way.
Each and every one is brought forth to serve the Buddhas, Constantly present in the morning within the Dharma King’s palace.
Rows upon rows of flowers made of the hundred jewels fly through the air, Praising the inconceivable in mid-sky.
If there are sentient beings who can cultivate weariness [with saṃsāra], they shall surely come in the future to the Pure, Unconditioned Vajra Terrace to expound the True Doctrine.
All Bodhisattvas from the Western Land will join together in ceaselessly scattering flowers as an offering; all shall be born upon these flowers, endowed with supernormal powers.
The fragrant aroma wafts in continuous succession; As flowers depart and flowers arrive, they grow ever more fresh.
At dawn, one constantly holds the offering from foreign lands; At mealtime, it returns before the World-Honored One.
In the first assembly, it removes distracted thoughts; In the second, its loud sound reaches all who have affinity.
The third resonance is soaring, capable of evoking sublime compassion; The fourth is a harmonious cry, truly pitiable [in its beauty].
The fifth causes the celestial Māras to tremble and disperse; It enables those who contemplate it to enter deep dhyāna.
Within these five assemblies of sound are ten kinds of benefits, Provided so that students may make their application of mind firm.
The Mani Jewel of the Five Assemblies of Wondrous Sound Can rain down the boundless wealth of the sublime Dharma;
The wise must certainly rely upon this for study. At the moment of death, with a single thought, one sits upon the lotus throne.
I address the great assembly gathered here now: The merit of mindfulness of the Buddha through the Five Assemblies is inexhaustible.
Today, those who practice together in this place of enlightenment, Shall surely escort one another to take their seats in the Lotus Palace.
The sacred teachings of the five assemblies are the True Vehicle; One shall certainly abandon Saṃsāra and escape the cage of suffering.
May all beings resolve their minds and turn their vows toward The Western World to attain supernormal powers.
The jewel trees stand in dense rows as a verdant forest; A gentle breeze produces fivefold harmonies of pure sound.
Flower rain falls at all times in every place; Those who see and hear it give rise to the true mind.
We, the assembly, now give rise to faith; We listen to the fivefold harmonies of Amitābha’s voice.
Dedicatedly seeking [rebirth], one shall not falsely assume a name; One will welcome the arrival at the Forest of Transformation in Ultimate Bliss.
The five assemblies join in resonance to praise the City of Purity; Towers and terraces grow lush, reflecting a greenish-blue against the clouds.
Boundaries are marked by lapis lazuli, the seven treasures, and golden cords; Everywhere, one hears only the sound of reciting the Buddha’s name.
The five assemblies of Amitābha are a boat and ship, Constantly ferrying beings across the ocean of suffering for eternal kalpas.
Provided they hear his voice, all shall attain liberation; They will surely transcend birth and death, departing from the realms of humans and devas.
These precious verses clearly transform sentient beings; The wondrous praise of the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra* is perfected within meditative concentration.
The Five-Session [Chanting] spreads widely throughout Jambudvīpa; We pledge to realize non-arising in Sukhāvatī.
This precious hymn to Amitābha is truly worthy of transmission; May it forever serve as a Dharma-boat for sentient beings.
Through the Buddha’s voice in the Five Sessions, śrāvakas attain liberation; In a single moment, they all sit upon golden lotuses.
In the west, five assemblies pervade the Sahā world; their intent is for sentient beings to practice much mindfulness of the Buddha.
In the Land of Many Treasures, billions of flowers bloom; those who hear his name and depart are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Thousands of kinds of music surround the golden terrace, and lotus flowers of a hundred jewels emerge from the water and open.
In the five assemblies, every sound must be chanted with urgency; at the moment of death, each one shall be welcomed.
The boundless transformation Buddhas with bodies of purple-gold will protect and transmit the Dharma to those who practice the Five Assemblies.
If one’s mindfulness of Amitābha does not regress, one will personally draw near to the swaying jeweled throne.
The five assemblies of Amitābha resound with majesty; The Great Sage transmitted them into this age of five turbidities.
Hearing their sound amidst the five sufferings, all attain bliss; By means of these five assemblies, one enters the Lotus Palace.
The Great Sage’s compassion opened the five assemblies; The intent of the five assemblies is to eliminate the five fires.
The five fires are extinguished by means of the five assemblies; All ride upon these five assemblies to transcend worldly toil.
The majestic resonance of the five assemblies is clear and profound; Like the rumbling of thunder, it articulates the wondrous sound.
The assembly of sages join together in praise, And all who hear it give rise to the aspiration for enlightenment.
The subtle five-toned sounds from the West shall come to save sentient beings in the five turbidities;
those who hear his name will all attain liberation. Through the five assemblies, they are led to the City of Precious Lotuses.
The clear and resonant five assemblies emerge from Mount Heng; their deep and solemn echoes now pervade the Five Regions.
The five assemblies all say that he will bring benefit and joy; Even in the age of the Dharma’s decline, he remains for another five hundred years.
Amitābha’s five assemblies penetrate the hearts of men; His voice of compassion for the sorrowful is winding and profound.
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* possesses such a sound; From the precious waters flows eternally the wondrous melody.
The resonance of the Five Assemblies rises and drifts through clouds and mists; Its pure tones, vast and brilliant, fill worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
If one can constantly recite them morning and night, One will dwell within the Buddha’s family life after life.
A fragrant breeze rises and touches the bodies of men, Blowing away the Five Assemblies to wash away greed and anger.
The five musical tones are further able to purify the five aggregates; hearing their names, one shall forever leave behind the clamor and dust of the world.

The drums and music, as well as the stringed songs of the Western Land, with lutes, flutes, and pipes blending together in harmony— each and every note proclaims the Dharma of the Five Assemblies, and every sound expounds the Six Pāramitās.
In the past, Śākyamuni was like an ordinary being; Through kalpas of ascetic practice, he guarded the *tathatā* and attained Buddhahood.
He has come and gone eight thousand times; Yet sentient beings have never left Jambudvīpa.
How truly bitter is the suffering of the people of Jambudvīpa! Generation after generation they pass one another by, sitting in endless lamentation.
Having briefly attained a human body, one departs once more; In a mere moment, a kalpa is fulfilled, and there is no returning.
The śramaṇa Lingzhen calls out from afar: Filled with weary resentment at impermanence within Jambudvīpa, I did not see the Tathāgata appear in the world;
Now, encountering the Dharma-ending age, I have fallen to the state of an ordinary person.
Self-reproaching, self-hating, and self-examining, The karmic obstacles of ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes are deep.
Life after life, one fails to transcend the three realms; Wandering through the six paths of rebirth until this very day.
Investigating the characteristics of the mind-nature with painful scrutiny, One seeks within the sacred teachings until they are perfectly integrated.
Though one has attained the status of a man and donned the Dharma robes, One cannot help but be born in the Age of Dharma Decline;
as the Age of Decline approaches, the distance from the Sages grows ever more remote. Among those who practice the gates of conduct, who alone can transcend?
In this present life, simply recite the name of Amitābha Buddha; This will also serve to extinguish the burning of the fire-hall of saṃsāra.
Mindfulness of the Buddha is the most urgent and essential gate; Once one has escaped Jambudvīpa, what more need be discussed?
If a person does not believe and harbors doubts, They should personally examine the holy teachings and verify the scriptural texts.
The scriptures exclusively urge mindfulness of Amitābha; There is no gateway more urgent or essential than this.
If one can have deep faith and no doubt, one shall immediately escape this Sahā world in this very life.
As proclaimed in the *Amitābha Sūtra*, by single-mindedly recollecting the Western Land for seven days,
the six ten-thousand *koṭis* of *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* Buddhas will praise one’s merit, declaring it to be immeasurable.
If for seven days one constantly recollects the Buddha in this manner, how much more so if one maintains it with a sincere heart until the end of one's life?
No other merits can compare to this; only the Buddha knows this gateway of swift liberation.
Sentient beings, examine and deliberate with earnest sincerity: the three miserable realms and the hells are difficult to endure.
Once lost, a human body may not be regained for ten thousand kalpas; why, then, do you not rejoice in going to the West?
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, there is perpetual joy; it surpasses heaven itself ten thousandfold.
I announce to all sentient beings: you must go there with haste! Why suffer through death while still lingering in Jambudvīpa?
In Jambudvīpa, the five turbidities prevail and poverty abounds;
All causes and conditions bring about the beginningless and endless suffering of the ocean, shoreless and bottomless. Myriad armies and multitudes are submerged within it;
The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss offers inexhaustible joy. The water-horses harmonize their voices to proclaim the Mahāyāna.
Bodhisattvas and devas do not suffer untimely death; Through mantras they attain Buddhahood—this is their final end.
The lands of Jambudvīpa are filled with pits and hollows; Mountains, peaks, and mounds are not level.
This is solely because the minds of people are largely unwholesome; All manner of mixed evils arise therein.
In the West, the Land of Ultimate Bliss is as level as the palm of a hand, Without a single mound, hillock, or pit;
The ground is made of lapis lazuli, bounded by golden realms, And multicolored lotus flowers grow everywhere.
The great oceans and many rivers of Jambudvīpa, Along with fish, turtles, crocodiles, and otters, are exceedingly numerous.
One morning, rain falls upon the valleys of Mount Heng; Drifting along, it mingles with various evils and sufferings.
In the West, within the seven-jeweled ponds of Sukhāvatī, The water of eight virtues has inconceivable depths;
Its shores have sands of gold, fragrant trees, And lotuses emerge through transformation, where transformed beings are born.
In Jambudvīpa, one receives retribution by entering a woman’s womb; The infant is wrapped within the two sacs, the outer and the inner, And though it reaches safety, it has not yet spoken.
For those with ignorance and attachment to self, the body follows them;
But in the Pure Land of the West, there are infants Who each receive their retribution by emerging from a lotus pedestal.
Having personally seen the Tathāgata preach the wondrous Dharma, one is naturally liberated and awakens to the opening of the mind.
The grasses, trees, and groves of Jambudvīpa—though tall, none exceed fifty fathoms;
they do not endure for many years, but wither and decay. Once their attachment has turned to ash and dust, they are no longer fit for use.

In the West lies the Forest of Seven Jewels in Sukhāvatī, Extending five million li upward, where even a faint breeze Stirs a thousand kinds of music, all proclaiming The Tathāgata’s voice of liberation.
In Jambudvīpa, people are scorched daily by the sun and wounded; They wander through saṃsāra in a twisting cycle, never finding permanence.
When appearing and disappearing, there are bright days and nights; yet the light obscured by wild clouds never fails.
The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss possesses boundless radiance, which likewise has no bright days or nights, remaining eternally constant.
Within a single pore of my Tathāgata, there is further a covering of light that pervades the ten directions.
Parents, wives, and children in Jambudvīpa—how long can one cherish them with incense and lamps?
Even if one attains reunion, it will not last; in an instant, separation is seen.
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, it is not like this; Amitābha Tathāgata is the Great Teacher.
For Bodhisattvas, humans and devas serve as noble friends; They share joy together without a moment’s separation.
In Jambudvīpa, suffering is extreme and boundless; The lives of men and women are bound by the ties of affection.
As evening falls, they seek much, fearing they will not survive; They have no leisure to return to the Truth or cherish virtuous conditions.
In the West, the joy of Sukhāvatī is boundless; There is no anxiety over men, women, or wealth.
If one requires fine silken robes, they arrive from a thousand li away; If one thinks of food, a hundred flavors appear by one's side.
The bodies of men and women in Jambudvīpa Are all alike, composed of the four great elements.
Binding hearts to one another creates hell; in an instant, one may sink into eternal oblivion for ten thousand kalpas.
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss there are no women; those born there all possess bodies identical to Bodhisattvas.
Having fully realized the three types of supernormal knowledge and the eight liberations, they are destined for Buddhahood in their next life, far removed from the clamor and dust of the world.
In this Jambudvīpa world, one may possess abundant wealth, yet each thing must be acquired through toil and returned through suffering.
Though one may use it to adorn the body, if no merit is cultivated, once the gates of the three miserable realms are closed, who will open them again?
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, there is joy beyond compare; do not look back upon the impure riches of Jambudvīpa.
When houses, gardens, and groves depart, they leave one behind; Clothing and a hundred flavors come according to one's desires.
The five turbidities of Jambudvīpa belong to ordinary people; Relying on karmic retribution, they cannot attain a body of autonomy.
Wives and children demand food and clothing from head to toe; Failing to discern the causes of these distinctions, they give rise to anger.
In the West, the Land of Ultimate Bliss, ordinary beings pass away; there they have no wives, children, or loving parents.
Those born there all ascend to the rank of Bodhisattvas and collectively realize the indestructible Vajra body.
In this Jambudvīpa world, one studies and practices dhyāna; yet it is a place of manifold evils, where the攀緣 (pān-yuan, *ālambana*) is abundant.
The wandering, wild mind is difficult to grasp, Like a boat tossed upon the great ocean.
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss it is not so; Those of the highest grade are born before the World-Honored One.
Having received a single word of instruction from me, the Tathāgata, They naturally awaken to the *Śatadharma-vidyāmukha* (The Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas).

In Jambudvīpa, he preaches the Dharma to deliver sentient beings; yet they merely listen to the words and phrases without practicing them, offering praise with minds full of attachment and raising their palms in greeting.
When encountering circumstances that conflict with their desires, ignorance arises.
In the Western Land, he preaches the Dharma to deliver sentient beings; there, waterfowl and birds sing melodies that resound through the void.
All who hear this say they shall take refuge in the Triple Gem; There is no other practice to be performed externally.
The world of Jambudvīpa cannot endure [this state]; Due to the karmic conditions of the West, the moon waxes month by month.
Even if one performs some small measure of good, One does not realize that hell is already being formed within a single moment.
The Pure Land of the West is truly a place where one may rest; For long kalpas, the sounds of suffering are never heard.
Drums, music, and songs fill the void, Each proclaiming the name of liberation.
Those in Jambudvīpa who hold the precepts yet lack wisdom Are like those walking in darkness during the day.
As he focused his mind forward, desiring to choose the path, Unaware, he lost his footing and fell into a deep pit.
In the West, the Land of Ultimate Bliss resounds with joy;
There, amidst the various sufferings and practices, he personally beheld Amitābha preaching the wondrous Dharma. Upon hearing it, he attained awakening and realized the end of ignorance.
Sentient beings recollecting the Buddha is like boarding a boat;
With the Tathāgata as the sovereign condition, they recite with single-minded focus for seven days and seven nights. This immediately counters the other mental factors for several hundred years;
If sentient beings wish to escape the cage of the mundane world, They must urgently and single-mindedly seek the merit of Buddha-recollection.
If one recites the name for seven days to be born in that land, it will certainly differ from other methods;
know only to practice mindfulness of the Buddha and do not give rise to doubt. Those who do not understand this are merely foolish;
it is solely for the sake of enabling swift transcendence, for ordinary beings in this world rarely possess such faith.
Sentient beings who mindfully recite the Buddha’s name will be welcomed by him; When impermanence becomes clear and distinct, they reach the Tathāgata’s abode in a mere snap of the fingers.
Traveling to other lands, they make offerings and realize non-arising;
In the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, they dwell forever in joy. How could that which Śākyamuni has spoken be a false transmission?
Exhort all sentient beings universally to be born in that land; How can one endure a painful death while longing for Jambudvīpa?
Focus the mind on the Buddha without distraction; One will certainly attain the Western Land and not waste one's efforts.
Even now, while still within the realm of ordinary beings, Upon the arrival of impermanence, one shall immediately obtain the six supernatural powers.
In the western land, within jeweled halls, ponds, and pavilions, The trees, waters, and birds understand human sentiment;
Parrots sing in harmony, praising the Triple Gem, And from their voices they manifest Mahāyāna sūtras.
In the west, the jeweled trees have precious roots and trunks, With precious flowers and jeweled nets most clearly displayed.
Rows upon rows of precious leaves interlace one another; precious leaves emerge in layers within a jewel-pool with jeweled banks and jeweled lotuses.
Upon jeweled steps and jeweled floors, beneath jeweled lotuses, sprouts grow spontaneously, even though there is no body from which they depart;
though there is no initial arousal of the thought of enlightenment, its buds arise of their own accord.
Ten billion flower banners encircle the golden pedestal;
upon a radiant jeweled throne, the Tathāgata sits and universally expounds the wondrous Dharma for all sentient beings, so that those who hear it awaken and their minds open.
Morning and evening, contemplate Amitābha, that he may descend to Jambudvīpa and subdue the hosts of Māras.
Having briefly traveled to the West to behold the Buddha in person, I have returned to deliver this Sahā world;
the Western Pure Land is most sublime. Music fills the air with myriad sounds, and clothing and food arrive naturally according to one's wishes;
even those who fear they will go hungry shall enjoy their fragrance.
In the western quarter, celestial robes rain down throughout the night; Within the jeweled palaces, they fly through the void following one’s person.
A hundred flavors arrive at a single thought-moment according to the mind; For what reason do so few sentient beings depart?
The vows and practices of Amitābha are vast and boundless; His compassionate salvation of all beings is universally and exhaustively merciful.
Desiring in general to transform and lead them back to their own land, The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
with great compassion, Is able to manifest wondrous and rare forms within the sea of suffering;
His golden-lotus body possesses the thirty-two marks, And upon his crown he bears the honored Amitābha.
The Bodhisattva Śrīkūṭa is most difficult to conceive; His body of purple-gold, its marks and signs complete and flawless.
A jeweled vase atop his head radiates brilliant light, Universally gathering those with the karmic affinity for mindfulness of the Buddha and rebirth in the Pure Land.
I rejoice that my past roots of merit are deep, Having encountered the sound of Amitābha’s pure teachings.
Holding fast to the Name without ceasing, when my life-span ends and I approach death, may my body be of purple-gold.
I have always lamented my own lack of diligent effort; now that I have heard this unsurpassed, pure, and true Dharma, we must together struggle against the confusion of ignorance.
I vow to utterly destroy it and attain the Golden Body.
In a single thought, concentrate the spirit and head toward the Jewel City; With the six supernormal powers, rouse the intent to learn lightness of body.
The feet tread upon thousand-petaled lotus flowers, And beneath the Moon-Bright Mānava tree, one walks within the subtle and profound Pure Land of Amitābha.
How could the people of this Sahā world ever know of that place?
Sunk for vast eons in the ocean of suffering, when will the time come to encounter rebirth?
In the precious land of Ultimate Bliss there is no decay; its jade-green towers and terraces arise spontaneously by divine power.
With mani-jewels, bright moons, and lapis lazuli waters, the light illuminating the ponds and pavilions is truly lovely.
The precious realm of Ultimate Bliss is most rare and wondrous;
Born into this world of jewels, I knew it not before, yet today I joyfully encounter the name of Amitābha. Those who suddenly renounce this Sahā world are few;
The precious realm of Amitābha is inconceivable— I can only lament that those who depart from the Sahā world are so rare.
Those in the Avīci Hell are called "The Departed"; once fallen there, for how many years can they ever emerge?
"Go back! Go back! they cry. In the five turbidities of Jambudvīpa, one is covered in the dust of defilements;
it is not like the place of happiness in the West, where upon arrival, the flower-thrones open at will.
Observing thoroughly that the three realms are entirely suffering, Ordinary beings are attached to trivial and fleeting matters;
Stirred by the waves of the karmic winds upon the ocean of desire, They emerge and submerge without ever pausing for a moment.
Sinking and drowning in the evil destinies for many kalpas, They occasionally travel once through the realms of humans and devas.
Through delusion, craving, and grasping, one clings to all states of existence; One wanders through the six realms of rebirth, dying and being born again.
Having ascended to higher realms, one returns once more to the lower;

Driven by karma, one enters a blazing pit ten thousand fathoms deep, Where sword-trees rend the body and shatter the heart and gallbladder— How could one endure having the tongue pulled out and plowed with iron plows?
Today, with utmost sincerity, I take refuge and pay homage To Amitābha, the two-legged illuminator of the world.
I pray that you will compassionately grant your acceptance; May your ray of light embrace me so that my potential may blossom.
May the sound of my name-recitation and mindfulness continue without interruption, And may the assembly of sages uphold me upon a pedestal of the seven treasures.
One can always look up with longing toward that land; at the end of life, the Buddha will surely come in person to welcome them.
The three realms offer no peace, like a house on fire; they are like a dusty open space at a crossroads.
One grows weary of dwelling among the bones and flesh of birth and death; how could one remain within the five aggregates or inside a womb?
Now, in this present life, having resolved to seek the Way, I encounter the rare opening of the Dharma-gate of the Pure Land.
I vow to reach the Western Land of Peaceful Nurturing, Where I may be escorted by Amitābha and the Holy Assembly.
Whether through meditative concentration or non-concentration, one can attain rebirth; Even those of the lowest grade, purified of dust and defilement, shall ascend the lotus dais.
Having attained the three knowledges (*tisro vidyāḥ*) and the eight liberations (*aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ*), you have long bid farewell to the five turbidities (*pañca kaṣāyāḥ*) and beheld the Tathāgata.
With one recitation of the Buddha’s name, one transformation-Buddha appears; from your mouth, red lotuses are born.
With a thousand recitations of the Buddha’s name, a thousand transformation-Buddhas appear, sitting cross-legged and upright before me.
Reciting the names of ten thousand Buddhas every day, Calculating the heights and depths of those Buddhas, I aspire to transcend the Brahma-heavens.
May I encounter all Buddhas at the moment of death, Who shall welcome me to the Pure Land to realize the Three Sages.
Comparing the merits of seated meditation with the praise of Buddha-recitation, The Tathāgata’s teaching is fundamentally non-dual.

It is simply that the minds of sentient beings are not impartial: One practices dhyāna with a resolute will to purify the mind through reciting the Buddha’s name, seeking only to be welcomed by an emanation Buddha;
One rides a carriage up the mountain, while another boards a boat upon the water. Though the heights and depths of the mountains and waters differ, [the destination remains the same].
First, it is able to eliminate the hindrance of sleep, causing the minds of all children to leave behind the veil of heavy darkness;
as the hindrances are extinguished, body and mind become pure, and one further beholds the western gate of a hundred jewels.
Second, it shakes and vibrates the realm of the heavenly Māras, causing the mind to be sent back to the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha.
If but the palaces of Māra hear this single thought, Through compassion, they shall forever serve the Compassionate Honored One for aeons.
The third sound pervades the realms of the ten directions, Causing all who have taken up evil to cease their suffering.
Each and every one who hears of Amitāyus Shall ascend to the Pure Land and dwell there in walking meditation.
Fourth: The profound sufferings of the three miserable realms cease; in an instant, they are transformed into precious lotuses.
All offenders sit amidst the flowers, and at that moment, hearing the Dharma, they realize non-arising.
Fifth: Do not allow external sounds to enter; let the mind go directly to the House of Dharma.
The radiant light shines eternally upon the lapis lazuli palace; Beings born by transformation scatter golden flowers like their own children.
In the sixth stage, the deluded mind is free from distraction; Within the visualization of Amitābha’s Pure Land, the jeweled forest is realized.
Amidst the trees, the wondrous Dharma is proclaimed; Every sound extols only the Mahāyāna sūtras.
Seventh, through courageous and diligent perseverance, the dust of ignorance is naturally eliminated;
in every thought-moment, one constantly contemplates the Land of Ultimate Bliss, as Maitreya, the Compassionate Lord, bestows a bright pearl.
Eighth, all Buddhas rejoice; they shall protect and mind those of faithful heart in the future.
Each and every one is caused to attain non-retrogression; At the time of death, they realize the purple-gold body.
Ninth, they are able to enter profound samādhi; In the tranquil, unconditioned, and outflow-free state of dhyāna-recollection, they see all Buddhas without thought.
They forever transcend birth and death, departing from the realms of humans and devas.
Tenth, by possessing all virtues, The fruits of merit and wisdom as numerous as the sands of the Ganges become perfectly clear and bright;
At the end of life, one sits upon a lotus flower in a pure land, Where Amitābha and his holy assembly personally come to welcome them.
The ground is made of lapis lazuli, reflecting the blue of the ponds; In every thought-moment, one must direct the mind toward that precious city.
The people of the eastern city are impoverished sons suffering in misery;
If you are born in the Ultimate Bliss, with trees and pearl necklaces, sentient beings, do not harbor doubt but recite the Buddha’s name. Determine upon the western seven-jeweled pond;
Recite the mantra ten million times every month as your daily practice, And dedicate the merit—Amitābha has already known this long ago.
The jeweled terraces and pavilions are most exquisite; upon reaching that Western Land, you shall know it for yourself.
Strive with diligence to turn your minds and recite the Buddha’s name; we shall meet together upon the lotus pedestals.
Amidst the pure ponds, jeweled lotus thrones stand, as fragrant forests in the Pure Land bloom under the sun.
The Great Compassionate Lord, majestic and golden-hued,
Gathers all who practice mindfulness of the Buddha to be reborn in Amitābha’s inconceivable Pure Land; Let those who seek this harbor no doubt in their hearts—
Like the sun emerging from clouds amidst the waves, they sit transcendent alone upon a precious lotus.
The Lord of Compassion in the Western Quarter is most majestic; how could ignorant people in this defiled age know him?
A tree formed from a hundred jewels rises a thousand feet high, Where mani-jewels and bright moons illuminate the golden pond.
Swans and cranes circle gracefully around the pool, While the devas sing praises in most pure and profound tones.
The flutes and pipes resound through the air as Brahma-sounds; those who hear them all flow together with the nature of reality (dharmatā).
The ponds, terraces, and towers are vast and exquisitely adorned; rows of precious jewel-trees form themselves naturally.
Clear waters flow eternally among the jade trees, and within the leaves of the crystal chimes, golden light is emitted.
Lotus flowers of the seven treasures emerge from the water; Their fragrant buds are now fully blossoming.
Progress in practice depends on one’s own application of the mind; Those who frequently recite the Buddha’s name will reach the purple-golden terrace.
People who recite the Buddha’s name and seek to go there Will arrive directly at the western pond of the seven treasures.
If you wish to know where suffering is most prevalent, there is none greater than the mud-plow hell.
Once a sinner enters it, they remain for kalpas as numerous as dust motes; their suffering from the very beginning is beyond remedy.
Thirsty, they drink molten copper; hungry, they climb sword-trees and cross the river of ashes amidst fierce flames.
May they leave this suffering behind and be born into peace and joy; May they seek rebirth in the Pure Land to behold Amitābha.
Contemplating hungry ghosts, one truly finds them pitiable:
Their entire bodies are ablaze with fierce fires, Their two ears cannot hear the word for "gruel," And their single bodies consist of nothing but skeletal lotuses.
Just as I was about to eat my food, it turned into fire; On the verge of drinking at a river, I saw a dried-up spring.
May I leave this suffering behind and be born in peace and happiness, To dwell forever in the West upon a precious lotus.
Lost on the path, once matched with the body of an animal, I have passed through many years, enduring bitter suffering.
In the bitter winter, dwelling in the open air amidst cold snow; In the sweltering summer, lying on the dusty streets under the dark sun;

With clothing made entirely of fur and skin, And regarding water and grass as the most precious of food and drink— May we leave this life of suffering for peace and happiness, To dwell forever in the West upon a precious lotus.
Although a human body is exceedingly difficult to obtain, Once attained, it gives rise to ten thousand kinds of sorrow.
At first, the rosy countenance is like a flower about to flourish; Suddenly, the hair turns white and the years become autumn.
Soul and spirit flee in terror as the body returns to the tomb; Life ends and form dissolves, the flesh becomes but dung in the earth.
Why do you not delight in birth in peace and bliss, But sit forever upon the golden terrace to roam the Buddha-lands?
The asuras are deceitful by nature and stubbornly arrogant; Their roots of goodness are all consumed by doubt.
Consequently, their bodies suffer like ghosts, Sinking into the dust and toil for long kalpas.
Falling into the realm of asuras due to a lack of faith, one suffers much from fighting and contention;
may you abandon doubt and be born in the Pure Land, where you shall forever draw near to Amitābha in the West.
The bliss of the devas is inconceivable, lasting for many births without end.
When this single lifetime’s retribution is exhausted, one encounters suffering once more;

Having abandoned that joy, one undergoes the five signs of decay, as foul-smelling sweat flows from every pore, And the flowers upon the crown on one's head wither away—this is entirely a place of impermanent transmigration.
It is not as good as sitting in the lotus ponds of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Concentrating the spirit, one dwells in a pure land within the subtle palace; The jeweled realm is filled with celestial flowers amidst the emerald groves.
The golden hall has opened and the Compassionate Lord smiles; Beholding His countenance, praise is inexhaustible.
Jeweled trees and tiered pavilions reflect one another’s light; All are the result of Amitābha’s power of vows.
In a single thought-moment, all shall go there; They must further obtain the six supernormal powers.
Carrying ten trillion robes in their laps, The assembly of sages, as numerous as motes of dust, receive offerings together.
From this point on, bowing the head, they gaze upon him constantly; They will surely abandon this Sahā world and escape the cage of suffering.
Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta are seen by people today; Each and every precious leaf and lotus flower is empty.
If you simply recite the name of Amitābha ten million times, Before long, you shall be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
First vow: May all sentient beings cultivate the Way universally. Second vow: May none give rise to doubt.
First, may the *kāṣāya* robe come to drape my body; Second, may I never again be born in a woman’s form;
Third, may I forever renounce cosmetics and perfumes; Fourth, may I appear with a plain face before the Tathāgata;
Fifth, may I be freed from the suffering of sins in the three miserable realms; Sixth, may I abandon and relinquish all stinginess regarding wealth.
Ninth, may sentient beings revere the Triple Gem; Tenth, may all Dharma gates be opened;
Eleventh, may sentient beings diligently practice mindfulness of the Buddha; Fourteenth, may they all gather before the Buddha to pay him homage;
Fifteenth, may they be reborn in the Pure Land of the West, Never again to undergo conception in Jambudvīpa.
Within the gate of Ultimate Bliss, the jewel-sun is full, Universally illuminating the three thousand and the great chiliocosm.
The Lord Amitābha, whose compassion extends far and wide, For your sake, once again opens the thousand-petaled lotus.
The jeweled pond and jeweled shores are exceedingly vast and level; The jeweled ground of lapis lazuli shines for a thousand fathoms.
Exhort all sentient beings everywhere to diligently recite the Buddha’s name; at the moment of death, He will surely come in person to welcome them.
The precious trees soak the heavens, their splendor beyond measure; one cannot fathom how many yojanas wide their blossoms and leaves extend.
In stillness, celestial music constantly resounds; when stirred by the wind, it is as clear and resonant as the distant sun and moon.
Seven rows of jewel trees with diverse and fresh radiance;
A single flower, a hundred yojanas in length and breadth, Upon which countless red lotuses bloom, and where all those born there dwell.
Within the light of the precious clouds, the morning mists appear; Upon the golden ground, celestial flowers rain down.
A gentle breeze stirs the trees of conditioned existence; The sound of the Dharma is subtle and peerless in its non-attachment.
You need only diligently recite the name of Amitābha Buddha; I shall now stay for a while to save the Sahā world.
Knowing that you deeply cherish me in your heart, If you encounter me once through the practice of nianfo, I shall pass by but once.
To escort me for a thousand li, you disregard all toil;
I do not know how, while sitting upright, you attained the white tuft-mark, From which countless Buddhas emerge. The jeweled throne upon the flower pedestal is naturally sublime;
No one has transcribed or praised it so that it might be transmitted. If it is not recited, how can it transform the world?
Go as you please to traverse the Land of Ultimate Bliss; I shall now depart for Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden.
Within that garden lies the Phoenix Pond, where the Tathāgata dwells and from his inconceivable golden mouth constantly proclaims the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
All who see or hear it cannot help but aspire to take refuge.
Having cultivated and perfected this karma, one sits in the western direction;
Boundless worlds are filled with golden light as mani-jewels flow into the lotuses. A single breeze stirs forth myriad fragrances;
Avalokiteśvara preaches the Dharma like a cascading torrent, While the voices of birds and celestial music blend in harmony.
Upon my ordinary twin lotus-feet, I wear a celestial crown atop my head;
Amitābha is upon me, clad in fresh robes of precious jewels. Beneath my feet are the thousand-spoked wheels, perfectly bright and radiant.
Do not crave the five desires of Jambudvīpa; by reciting my name, you shall swiftly achieve realization.
Having realized truth, one early attains the realization of non-action (*wuwei*);
The majestic marks and radiant light settle upon the two eyebrows, capable of illuminating all the defiled lands of Jambudvīpa.
Transforming them into Buddha-lands of wondrous brilliance, this subtle and exquisite radiance dwells among humanity; Universally gathering all sentient beings, it leads them before the Buddha.
Each and every one attains the rank of Bodhisattva, Simultaneously all gaining seats upon red lotuses.

The red lotuses grow from jeweled flower ponds; A thousand lights and ten thousand colors, inconceivable, With water-birds, pearl forests, and the same pure land, Exquisite fragrances and music accompany them at all times.
Together we have all arrived at the Palace of Sublime Flowers;
From the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, the great heroes all come to welcome us to the precious halls. They praise our diligent merit from beginning to end;
This constancy from start to finish is inconceivable. We sit upon jeweled lotus pedestals within the crystal pools.
This was created by the power of your firm resolve; it has nothing to do with the Buddhas acting for you.
Because your vow-power is exceedingly firm and strong, you shall certainly be born in the Highest Grade and sit upon the Vajra-throne.
Do not decline to remain for a while in the realm of Jambudvīpa; your name as it stands now shall reside in the Western Land.
The jeweled palace in the western quarter is made of mani;
its ground and pathways are of gold and lapis lazuli, with a thousand-petaled lotus seat of a hundred jewels.
The Dharma-body is pure, draped in garments of pearls and jewels, radiating myriad lights from every part of its body as it wanders through seven rows of precious trees.
Do not be surprised by this subtle and wondrous praise of the Lotus Jewel; it transforms and delivers sentient beings without concealment.
If one conceals these subtleties, one cannot become a teacher. As the Dharma teachings circulate, they neither flourish nor decline.
For your sake, I have extensively proclaimed this praise of Ultimate Bliss; the Tathāgata’s words manifest as divine majesty.
Divine majesty pervades the Dharma-realm, saving all living beings; The physical eye is opened anew, and the wisdom-eye shines clearly.
Sitting upright, one can behold the Land of Ultimate Bliss; Its towers and terraces are all made of jewels.
Recite, recite! The jeweled ground is like a thousand suns; Amidst those thousand suns, ten thousand colors of light radiate.
Within the light are countless Bodhisattvas; Before the feet of Amitābha they offer sublime incense.
From that sublime incense clouds of jewels arise; The Bodhisattvas, dignified and majestic, pay their respects with no slighting manner.
Before the towers, celestial music plays its wondrous sounds; One hears only the voices of water-birds chanting the Buddha’s name.
The Buddha’s voice shook the palace of Yama; the hearts and livers of the celestial Māras were entirely melted down.
Having been subdued, the Māra armies followed behind the Buddha, prostrating with such devotion that their number was infinite.
These countless great Māra armies all at once attained rebirth as human beings.
In total, I dedicate my mind to be reborn in that land, Respectfully and diligently gazing upon the Great Compassionate Honored One.
The Honored One’s wondrous form is most majestic and sublime; His magnificent radiance is like five Mount Sumerus.
His two eyes are clear and bright like the great ocean; He possesses the great compassion of the Forty-Eight Vows.
With great compassion, you widely open the gate to the Land of Ultimate Bliss; You vow to save the people of the five turbidities in Jambudvīpa.
To each you grant the radiance of the seven treasures and a jeweled seat; How could one ever again perceive even a single mote of dust?
From the mind, Buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust appear, And boundless worlds manifest in diverse splendors.
The five aggregates transform into pure eyes, And the eight consciousnesses turn into eight ponds of virtue;
These eight ponds are all jeweled lotus flowers, Where those who recite the Buddha’s name sprout the buds of the Way.
Throughout the entire defiled and evil realm of Jambudvīpa, All at once receive the refined essence of Sukhāvatī.
Within the Garden of Essence, I behold the Tathāgata, Each seated upon a radiant platform of the seven treasures.
Fortunate to have been born together in the land of the Compassionate Lord, Throughout long kalpas, I shall never again turn back.
Never turning back, I dwell forever for hundreds of thousands of eons in the West, Where majestic marks and radiance equal those of the sun and moon.
Within the gate of forbearance lies the Eightfold Noble Path; amidst sound, fragrance, and wind are the Seven Factors of Enlightenment.
Within the path of enlightenment dwells the Honored One of Purity; the profound and wondrous awakening is difficult to discourse upon.
By eliminating conceptualization, one spontaneously achieves liberation; by comprehending the mind, one can open the gate of great compassion.
The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss has been clarified since ancient times;

All phenomena arise from the mind—by gathering the thoughts, the mind becomes tranquil and bliss is attained. By contemplating the Buddha with certainty, the precious platform will come to welcome you back;
Who then would wish to undergo the cycle of rebirth in the West?
Let us together recite the name of that Amitābha; Reborn in Sukhāvatī, sit upon the transformation platform.
Come, let us go! This Sahā world is filled with suffering and hardship;
Hasten your hands and focus your mind to recite the name of that Buddha. The Dharma-gate of Amitābha’s Pure Land is now open.
Return! Who here can endure such calamity?
All you fellow practitioners who share this same affinity, exert yourselves together and return!
