Let us all together be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss, and offer special flowers to that Tathāgata.
Return! Return! Birth, old age, sickness, and death press on with their suffering;
day and night you must diligently contemplate that Buddha. In the blissful seclusion of the Pure Land, one sits upon a jeweled terrace.
Return! Return! In this world of Saha, there is only wailing and lamentation.
Urgently and single-mindedly recite the name of Amitābha Buddha; Permanently part from the five turbidities and behold the Tathāgata.
Come back! Come back! The Dharma-gate of Amitābha’s Pure Land is now open.
If you have even a moment’s need and can recite the Buddha’s name, At the end of life, you will certainly sit peacefully upon the transformation platform.
Return! Return! Day and night you hear the chanting: "Alas!
Strive with all your might to turn the mind and return to the Pure Land; pay homage to the Tathāgata in the Maṇi Palace!
Return! Return! This defiled realm of Saṃsāra cannot be endured.
Hasten your hands and must return to the Land of Peace and Bliss; To see the Buddha and hear the Dharma, where the five [aggregates] are non-arising—go back and come forth!
The three miserable realms and the hells are truly pitiable;
Through thousands of births and ten thousands of deaths there is no rest, As for many kalpas one is constantly burned by fierce flames.
With every sound, recite the name of Amitābha; All who hear it at once shall sit upon the golden platform.
Come back! The mountain of knives and forest of swords are truly difficult to endure;
Those who drink wine, eat meat, and crave wealth and beauty Shall cast their bodies into the boiling cauldrons for long kalpas.
It is not like the joyful realms of the West, Which eternally transcend birth and death and are free from impermanence.
The Dharma-treasury’s causes involve weighty and solemn vows; Śākyamuni’s compassionate vows are inconceivable.
Exhort the assembly and urge them to seek [the Way] without interruption; Do not let them waste their efforts by delaying the arousal of the bodhicitta.
With the great compassion of the Forty-Eight Vows, I only regret that sentient beings are slow to recite the Buddha’s name.
May all who suffer among these vows be able to go there, Precisely when Amitābha appears in the world.
Upon his head, millions of spiraling shells manifest, And beneath his pair of feet, he treads upon lotus flowers.
If you but single-mindedly and diligently recite the Buddha’s name, His compassionate light will directly enter the practitioner’s home.

How excellent is the Śākyamuni, the Tamer of Men! He exhorts the multitude to constantly uphold this pure dharma-gate, causing all the devas in the void to offer praise, so that the suffering of sentient beings may end and they emerge from the thick darkness.

May all those seated here swiftly arouse the resolve for enlightenment; You must enter deeply into the hundred dharma-gates and listen to the true teachings of the Compassionate Honored One. Now, you students, do not hesitate;
I exhort you to cultivate the path with diligent and earnest effort, For you must profoundly loathe this great fiery pit of Jambudvīpa.
Upon the golden ground, lapis lazuli reflects; The bright moon and mani-jewels arise at will.
The Samādhi of Amitābha is naturally serene and pure; Yet sentient beings with karmic obstructions do not hear its name.
When water, birds, and forest trees all preach the Dharma, Those with distracted body and mind are invaded by demons.
Amitābha, the Great Awakened One, is a skilled physician; He is well able to treat the thieves that afflict all living beings.
By repenting, one expiates the ten evils within the body; Now is precisely the time to ascend the lotus throne.
Amitābha originated this teaching in the Western Land; It has now been transmitted to arrive in the Great Tang.
Within the world of the five turbidities, you stir up the Pure Land; upon the paths of the three miserable realms, you erect ferries and bridges.
You reveal the gates of teaching with utmost swiftness, urging others through skillful means to scatter flowers and incense.
Through the contemplation of the ultimate, one meets [the Buddha] within the mind; the karmic defilements of Jambudvīpa naturally vanish away.
Practitioners, exert yourselves and earnestly exhort others to contemplate the Buddha; Upon seeing the Buddha, you shall be born upon a terrace of the seven treasures.
If for a single thought-moment you harbor doubt and fail to give rise to faith, You will be transmigrated through the three miserable realms for ten thousand kalpas.
The initial gateway to the Pure Land may seem broad and easy to enter, But seeking refuge and repenting becomes increasingly difficult.
To repay those who harbor doubts and slander through [this] manifested transformation, come here together to behold the shattering of the body.
Observe how exceedingly tranquil is the world of Amitābha; all who have faith must examine it with discernment.
Although the Buddha’s body with its marks and signs is seen in its entirety, one should specifically focus the contemplation upon the white tuft of hair between his brows.
In the western realm of the Jewel World, the city of Vaiśālī, The ponds and terraces of the seven treasures are all places where beings are born by transformation;
Within the Garden of Joy the Buddha preaches the Dharma, And amidst the trees of sorrowlessness, birds discourse upon the sutras.
Avalokiteśvara, with his marks and signs of excellence, destroys all heterodoxies, Gathering in all living beings to bring them into the Buddha’s household.
For seven days, practice the visualization of the Ultimate Land of Bliss; Once the visualization is perfected, you shall immediately sit upon a lotus flower.
The Unborn Land of Bliss is truly worthy of seeking; Those who go with a single-minded heart—do not be dilatory!
Samādhi will be attained suddenly according to one's thought; This is how the vows of Avalokiteśvara flow forth.
The jeweled towers of the Western Pure Land stand high; Those who go with a single-minded resolve need not lament their toil.
With one thought of right contemplation, you shall arrive at once; Upon arrival, first ascend the purple-gold bridge.
I have secretly observed that the karmic offenses of those in the human world are many; Yet they create them for themselves and also incite others to do so.
Craving wealth and beauty, one finds no joy; One refuses to recite the name of Amitābha from the mouth, And throughout the day indulges in meat and blood.
Taking the lives of others without compassion, The Buddha says there is no enmity that goes unrequited:
In the three miserable realms, one shall again be boiled in cauldrons of boiling water.
The mountain of blades with its ten thousand edges is as smooth as silver; The sword-trees with their thousand peaks are fresh with frost and snow.
The fierce flames of the blazing furnace never cease; It awaits those from Jambudvīpa who eat flesh.
In the West, the path to enlightenment excels that of Sahā; There, the five desires and malevolent demons have no foothold.
To achieve Buddhahood, one need not labor through various good deeds; Sitting upright upon a lotus pedestal, one simply recites the name of Amitābha.
Sentient beings in the five turbidities mostly fall back;
It is better to recite the Buddha’s name and go to the Western Land, Where one will naturally attain perfect enlightenment, And return to the sea of suffering to serve as a bridge for others.
The Dharma King universally exhorts us to mind Amitābha; his intent is for all beings to emerge from the river of craving.
Those who behold the Compassionate Lord upon the superior lotus pedestal have all attained it through much mindfulness of the Buddha.
Now Amitābha wishes to travel throughout the ten directions, with banners, streamers, and precious canopies leading the way before him.
In the sky, the Bodhisattva utters a Brahma-like voice, praising: "In the Land of Ultimate Bliss, what further cause for sorrow?
The color of the kalaviṅka bird is most exquisite;
furthermore, there is the king of birds, the peacock, whose song resounds day and night without ceasing, constantly sighing that sentient beings dwell in the realms of suffering."
Jeweled towers, jeweled pavilions, and jeweled clouds interlaced; Upon a vast, level ground, a hundred jeweled gates stand open.
The Compassionate Lord ascends His jeweled throne facing the sun; With jeweled hands, He constantly beckons those who recite the Buddha’s name.
You all must not shrink from the pain of shattering your bodies; When ignorance is utterly dispersed, the sprouts of goodness will grow.
Evil karma and the six sense-objects naturally cease; One wanders freely through the Pure Land with a joyful mind.
The mark of the white tuft of hair is most distinct; A hundred billion emanations appear to transform all sentient beings.
Exert yourselves with a diligent heart and frequently recite the Buddha’s name; The holy assembly of the West will come to welcome you.
The Purple Terrace and Golden Pavilion with nets of pearls, And jeweled banners high and manifest beyond the clouds— All who possess the karmic affinity may go there;
Together, let us cross the Bridge of Dharma.
If one carefully investigates the various holy teachings, One will find that the principle of mindfulness of the Buddha is most capable of growth.
With little effort, one shall achieve accomplishment; at the time of death, the holy assembly will personally welcome one to that Western Realm of Peaceful Nurturing.
There, joy and bliss shall be eternal and free from sorrow;
in every thought, merit alone shall increase and flourish, so that birth, old age, sickness, and death shall forever cease.
The sentient beings of that land are ever joyful; The three evil realms and the six paths are never heard of there.
In a single thought-moment, they listen to the assembly together; Hearing one teaching, they awaken to hundreds of thousands of gates.
The Western Pure Land is truly a place where one may dwell; If you wish to seek rebirth there, arouse a sincere heart.
Amitābha has sent me to call out your names; you must simply focus your mind with single-minded devotion for the rest of your life.
Do not be lax—suddenly you must recite the Buddha’s name! If you wish to transcend the sea of suffering, you must have a boat;
by calling his name, you will certainly be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss, forever severing the stream of birth and death in Jambudvīpa.
Among all myriad practices, this is the most urgent and essential; Nothing is more swift than the gateway of the Pure Land.
Not only did our Original Teacher speak these words with his own mouth, But all Buddhas of the ten directions collectively proclaim this teaching.
Do not decline to recite the Buddha's name throughout the day; Amitābha’s original vow permits you to be invited.
At the moment of death, one shall be born in peace and bliss; Hearing the Dharma and attaining realization, one finds liberation.
The Western Land of Ultimate Bliss resounds with joy; Those who hear this turn their minds and vow to be reborn there.
Though the distance of the path is unknown, The Tathāgata personally comes to welcome them.
By the power of the Compassionate One’s vows, the Western Land is established;
The azure heavens are adorned with seven treasures, while coral is scattered as decoration across the steps and terraces. The ground is spread with pure gold, a deep and vibrant yellow;
The cool waters of virtue are strewn with golden sand, Where shadows mingle with auspicious clouds like fragments of brocade and rosy dawn.
Let not the assembly speak of the Dharma as empty; From above, heavenly flowers fall at times.
In that land, a gentle breeze blows through the jeweled groves, Whispering a thousand varieties of sounds that carry the resonance of the Dharma.
Beside the lion throne, white jade is refined; Where devas and humans walk, the steps are paved with gold.
In the western direction, the day lasts for an eon; The opening and closing of the lotus flowers are most distinct.
All you multitudes, mindful of the Buddha, seek samādhi; Upon the purple-gold pedestal lies the True Name.
The Tathāgata’s teachings are vast and boundless; He delivers those with whom he has affinity according to their capacities, great or small.
Eighty-four thousand beings are all liberated; The gateway of mindfulness of the Buddha is swift beyond compare.
The lifespan of Amitābha is truly boundless; His light shines without obstruction upon worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Each and every one who receives this light is gathered and sustained; In birth after birth, they forever sit upon precious lotus flowers.
Lotus buds fill the Western Quarter; within the ponds, wild ducks, geese, and mandarin ducks each utter their cries as they preach the Dharma.
Every flower and every stalk wafts fragrance through the air, where a rain of blossoms swirls and descends in profusion, scattering coral upon the ground to form natural pedestals.
The wind blows, and fallen leaves fly away; it blows away withered flowers, yet they come back again.
The six sense-faculties delusively grasp at all objects of perception; thus, samādhi cannot manifest.
Diligently brandish the sword of light to slay the thief of ignorance; swiftly lead one another upward onto the precious lotus.
The name of Amitābha is inconceivable; Those who hear it should know that their sins are extinguished.
To merely recite the name and be born in the Pure Land— All must have deep faith and harbor no doubt.
If one person in this world recites the Buddha’s name, A lotus flower will immediately appear in the West.
Provided that one remains ever non-retrogressive while seated, A single flower reaches this place to welcome you;
The pure waters of the pond reflect the lotus dais, And the dense, jeweled temple opens wide toward heaven.
The towering Lord of Compassion always smiles; Everyone is gathered to be received into rebirth.
Do not be surprised that I repeatedly urge you so earnestly; I see that when people pass away, they have no place to go.
If one can attain the profound samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha, One need not fear the King of Equality in the future.
A thousand layers of fragrant trees and ten thousand layers of incense Reflect their light upon the seven-jeweled sands within the pond.
Precious sands gush forth with mani-jewel water; The flowing streams are pure and flawless wherever they reach.
A net of indranīla pearls and purple-gold light Shines upon halls of the seven treasures, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Each flower brings forth all Buddha-lands, And every sound praises that Western Quarter.
Upon the lapis lazuli ground stands the Purple Gold Mountain, its flying colors and flowing rosy clouds reflecting throughout the world.
Sentient beings in the five turbidities suffer much from feverish affliction, while the Western Pure Land is exceedingly tranquil and free.
Within the jeweled ponds are flower pedestals, and inside the Amitābha Hall, light is emitted and spread.
You sentient beings, diligently recollect the Buddha; Exhausting your lives in the three realms, you shall be reborn in the Western World.
This is most excellent; with focused mindfulness, look up toward the precious city.
Because of the profound and far-reaching merit of this contemplation, You shall realize non-arising within the Lotus Assembly.
Behold that realm of Amitābha’s Sukhāvatī, A vast, level city of myriad jewels, Arising through the adornment of the forty-eight vows;
Surpassing all other Buddha-fields, it is most sublime.
The multitudes from the great oceans of other lands, Though they calculate for an entire kalpa, cannot know its name.
Exhort everyone universally to return to the West and join that assembly;
The *saṃsāra*-like samādhis will naturally be perfected, And the precious land of non-arising shall forever be free from impermanence. From every jewel flows countless rays of light;
The practitioner must keep their mind constantly before their eyes, So that the supreme deity leaps for joy and enters the Western Land.
Jeweled ponds radiate jewel-colored light; from each ray of light arise countless terraces.
Within each terrace are thousands of billions of jewel pavilions, surrounded on all sides by ten billion jewel banners.
There are jewel trees and jewel groves, with jewel flowers, jewel leaves, and jewel roots and stalks.
Some forests consist of a thousand jewels, while others are formed of a hundred jewels;
their rows stand in perfect alignment, and their leaves follow one another in succession. Their colors are each distinct, as is their radiance;
they are all equal in measure, rising thirty thousand [yojanas] high. When their branches and leaves touch one another, it is said to be without cause.
The jewel-pools have jewel-banks and golden sand; with jewel-leaves, jewel-canals, and jewel-lotuses, they extend twelve yojanas in perfect symmetry.
Jewel-awnings, jewel-nets, and jewel-railings surround them;
the waters of the Tathāgata’s virtues flow along, following the jewel-trees. Amidst the waves, one experiences joy, yet perceives fear.
I send word to those with affinity who travel this path together: Exert yourselves to overturn delusion and return to your original home.
The King of Flowers, Amitābha’s Original Vow, sits enthroned;
All manner of jewels form his city, and atop its terraces four banners unfurl in radiant splendor. Amitābha sits alone, manifesting his true form.
Amitābha’s body and mind pervade the Dharma-realm, Manifesting as reflections within the thoughts and minds of sentient beings.
Therefore, I exhort you to constantly observe: From the mind arises thought, which manifests his true countenance.
His precious face and precious form sit upon a lotus flower; When the mind opens, one beholds the adornments of the Land of Waves.
The flowers of the three bodies abound upon the jewel trees, And the sound of wind-chimes resonates with the sacred texts.
The body of Amitābha is like a mountain of gold; His marks and signs and radiant light illuminate the ten directions.
Only those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha are gathered by his light; One should know that the Original Vow is most powerful.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions extend their tongues as witness; By single-mindedly reciting the Name, one reaches the West.
There, amidst the flowers, the wondrous Dharma is revealed, And the vows and practices of the ten stages manifest spontaneously.
The entire dharma-realm trembles from afar like whirling tumbleweeds, As transformation-buddhas gather like clouds, filling all of space.
I universally exhort all who have the karmic affinity to constantly maintain mindfulness, To forever sever the womb-birth and realize the six supernormal powers.
Sitting upright in the full lotus posture, enter into samādhi;
Visualize the mind and bring it to the Western Land, Where you behold Amitābha and the realm of Ultimate Bliss, Adorned with the seven treasures throughout the earth and the void.

The body of Amitābha is infinitely vast; yet he repeatedly exhorts sentient beings to contemplate his smaller form, manifesting at will as sixteen or eight feet in height according to their capacities.
His circular halo equally reveals the true and the transformed before them.
Those of the highest grade, the highest practice, and the sharpest faculties who seek rebirth in the Pure Land transcend both greed and anger.
According to the distinctions in practice, there are three grades; through the five gates in continuous succession, one assists the three causes.
Whether for one day or seven days, one applies oneself with diligent effort; until the end of life, one ascends the platform to transcend the six sense objects.
How joyful it is to have encountered this rare opportunity! One shall forever realize the unconditioned Dharma-nature body.
The person of middle capacity within the middle grade of the middle rebirth, having observed the one-day fast and dwelt upon golden lotuses,
honors their parents and dedicates the merit; for them,
the Buddha and the assembly of śrāvakas gather to explain the causes for the bliss of the Western Land, until they reach the side of Amitābha’s flower-throne.
A flower-cage of a hundred jewels remains for seven days; The three grades of lotuses bloom,

attesting to the Lesser Truth for those of the lower grade, lower conduct, and lower faculties— Those who commit the ten evils and the five heinous crimes, who harbor greed and anger, violate the four grave precepts,
steal from the Sangha, and slander the True Dharma, Yet have never felt shame or remorse for their past transgressions.
All those suffering from their karmic retributions gather like clouds;
before the fierce fires of hell reach the sinner, he suddenly encounters a spiritual friend who has attained rebirth there.

Urgently exhorted to single-mindedly recite the name of that Buddha, the manifested Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arrive at his voice. After a single moment of mindfulness, his mind enters a precious lotus.
The three flowers of obstruction remained closed for many kalpas; it was only at this time that the cause of bodhicitta first arose.
How could one delight in the inconceivable truth of dharmas? Having met no Bodhisattvas as fellow students, the Tathāgata Nature-Ocean became my sole teacher.
Thirsting to hear Prajñā, I have abandoned all thought of worldly drinks.
Mindfulness of non-arising cuts off hunger; all adornments are explained as the Dharma.

Without a mind to receive them, one naturally knows; entering the flower-pool of the seven factors of enlightenment at will, one concentrates the spirit on the single branch of the eight liberations. Bathing body and crown in the heart-water of Amitābha.

The Great Sage Avalokiteśvara bestowed his robe upon him; Desiring to ascend to the supreme void and roam the Dharma-realm, he was granted the prediction of enlightenment in an instant, named "The Unconditioned.
In such a state of distant travel and joy, Śākyamuni’s compassionate heart pervades the entire Dharma-realm, Universally cherishing all sentient beings, even the most minute and moving creatures.
I desire to transform them all so they may attain liberation;
Because sentient beings’ karmic offenses lack common affinity, I teach them collectively to take refuge in the Pure Land; For Amitābha had affinities established in former lives.
It is not only the people of Sahā who go alone; Those departing for other directions are likewise infinite.
Amitābha’s vow to gather and transform beings without weariness, His compassionate heart constantly wanders through the world.
If there is one who can recite the Buddha’s name with sincere devotion, His white light will shine directly before their eyes.
The beings as numerous as motes of dust throughout the worlds of the ten directions— May they all, at the same moment their lives end, be born [in his land].
Calculated according to the mental inclinations and desires of those sentient beings, he manifests divided bodies everywhere to welcome and receive them all at once.
Observing that Amitābha and his retinue have long planted vast causes throughout past kalpas, both ordinary and holy beings alike possess the same marks and signs;
humans and devas alike share this single body of purple-gold.
Jeweled trees, jeweled towers, and soaring jeweled pavilions; jeweled ponds, jeweled grounds, and lotus lands formed of jewels fill the void with worthy sages.
Within these flowers dwell all those born by transformation;
Amitābha attained the Way ten kalpas ago, and all sentient beings aspire to go to the Western Land.
Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas are beyond calculation; how could sages with the five supernatural powers fathom those inhabitants of that land?
Dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression, they have forever transcended birth and death and severed impermanence.
As the nine grades of lotuses bloom, they are liberated early; what prevents them from attaining realization with serene composure?
The Bodhisattva path is perfected solely for the sake of sentient beings; since beings have not yet matured, it is difficult to achieve enlightenment.
Thus, he dwells in Tuṣita to cultivate the conditions for transformation, descending at intervals to contemplate the world with a focused mind.
Only when the human lifespan reaches eighty thousand years will he attain enlightenment; in three assemblies, meeting those with the necessary conditions, he leads them to realize Nirvāṇa.
Together we dedicate our minds to be born in the Pure Land;
at the moment of death, we shall go as we wish to behold the Buddhas of the ten directions throughout the triple world, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Their perfected merit is uniform and flawless, and the adornments of their lands are all of one kind; thus we must together praise the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
All who hear his name shall surely go [to liberation]; The name "Liberation" is certain—how could its attainment be delayed?
The Tathāgata does not perish; he has entered parinirvāṇa. He dispatches his relics throughout the three thousandfold world-system.
Stūpas and pagodas are erected in his likeness; One pays homage, recites his name, burns incense, and offers the hundred-fold blended perfumes.
Although the sublime practices of Bodhisattvas are immeasurable, you should know that mindfulness of the Buddha is foremost.
By means of this causal condition, one is born in the Pure Land and reaches the presence of the World-Honored One in an instant.
The subtle words of the Tripitaka and the true teachings of the Sages are difficult to encounter, difficult to pass through, and indeed difficult to meet again.
Passing through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, One knows there exists the gateway to the Western Pure Land.
In a single thought-moment, one must give rise from the mind to transcend birth and death; Throughout one's life, never retreating, the Buddha welcomes the soul.
Avalokiteśvara rescues and gathers many with ease; His supernatural powers and transformations are truly inconceivable.
Some may further transform their bodies to attain perfect enlightenment, while others serve as attendants, manifesting the relationship of teacher and disciple;
for the desires of sentient beings are not uniform, they respond to conditions within the six realms according to what is timely and appropriate,
exhorting and guiding them all back to the Pure Land, so that all may behold the Buddha and realize the unconditioned.
Śrī-Ābhāsvara-dhara dwells in the Land of Amitābha; Having attained a peerless body of purple-gold through karmic retribution, he comes to this realm to deliver sentient beings.
Manifesting a form identical to those of this world, he takes pity on the suffering of the burning house;
Following the conditions of the six paths, he forcibly draws them forth.
Send them toward the peaceful land in the west, To sever the causes and conditions of birth and death.
The sages and saints of the Pure Land in the west possess Unsurpassed mastery of supernatural powers;
With a single thought, they travel together through Buddha-fields, Passing through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all offer worship; Simultaneously they preach the Dharma, and at once it is heard.
The Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in worlds as vast as motes of dust— Whose six supernormal powers and divine functions can ever be fully known?
Having heard of that Land of Peace and Bliss, Amitābha’s realm, All are filled with yearning and offer their most earnest devotion.
How much more so for ordinary beings wandering in saṃsāra, who do not seek liberation from worldly glory?
Even if one were to calculate for eons the multitude of beings throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time,
how could they ever know the skillful transformations of the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, which lead all to the ultimate fruit and sever greed and delusion?
Pointing toward the Western Land of Peace and Bliss, All who hear its name regret their own slow progress toward rebirth there.
Those who have attained liberation all aspire to it with joy; If ordinary beings do not go, what would they be doing?
Excellent is the power of the Dharma General’s contemplation, By which he beholds the jeweled net canopy of Amitābha.
The pure lands of all Buddhas manifest from the mind; sentient beings must always look inward.
Amitābha dwells within the purple-gold tower, where Bodhisattvas and sages of the ten directions roam.
In a single thought-moment, they hear the wondrous Dharma from other realms; having forever bid farewell to the sea of suffering, what further cause for worry could there be?
Alas! The ocean of suffering is truly vast and deep; One must simply resolve the mind upon Amitābha, Day and night, with a devoted heart, dwell constantly in mindfulness.
At the moment of death, a single thought can transcend Saṃsāra;
This Jambudvīpa is foul and evil, unfit to remain in, For there are pits of fire a myriad fathoms deep that burn one’s very being.
Quickly and with single-minded devotion, contemplate that Buddha; Awaken to non-arising within the precious realm of Amitābha.
In the gate of Sukhāvatī, amidst the seven-jeweled ponds, The lotus blossoms with the radiance of purple-gold.
With a moment’s thought of Amitābha, one ascends the jeweled terrace; In an instant, before one realizes it, the unconditioned is realized.
Before the Jade Green Tower stands a terrace of the seven treasures; The youths of the various heavens vie with one another to come and behold it.
Having obtained golden flowers, they offer them to the Buddha; Everywhere they speak only of "Excellent!
Amitābha dwells within the jeweled city tower; With hearts turned toward him, they seek him in every thought, facing west.
Having attained the three vidyās and the eight liberations, One bids eternal farewell to the five turbidities; what further cause for sorrow?
At the fifth assembly, one must doubly revere him; By chanting his name and contemplating the purple-golden [Amitābha], One discerns the heterodox from the orthodox within the mind.
When contemplating the objective realm, it does not come to invade; In the jeweled groves of Ultimate Bliss, A subtle breeze sounds with the voice of the fifth assembly.
Within the sounds, the wondrous Dharma is expounded; those who listen awaken to non-arising.
In the pure land, the jewel groves resound with the fivefold assembly of Amitābha; those who hear them all give rise to joy.
Passing by the banks of the white jade pond, the fragrance emanates from within the lotus petals; amidst the void, the Brahma-sounds unfold.
For five long kalpas one dwells constantly, Temporarily arriving at the jeweled city towers; Wandering at ease, what need for worry?
Hearing only the recitation of the Five Assemblies— Throughout the long kalpas, what further cause for sorrow? The precious lands abound in true realms, Proclaiming the sounds of the Five Assemblies;
One constantly hears the resonance of solemn purity, From which it gradually becomes more profound and deep.
The golden trees of Ultimate Bliss Blossom with the sounds of the five assemblies;
They intend to cause all who hear them to practice fully. Holding lotuses of the nine grades, These flowers receive those who are reborn there.
As the sounds of the five assemblies resonate one after another, From this point on, the dust of worldly defilements is washed away. Who among us is not a child of Ultimate Bliss?
Born within the petals of the lotus, This is due to having heard the fivefold assembly [of mantras]. From this point, the glory of worldly dust ceases;
In the Pure Land, mani-jewel waters Flow in channel upon channel everywhere. The sound of the water contains the fivefold assembly;
The towering Amitābha has already subdued the Māra of birth and death. Such is the land of jeweled ponds and pearl forests.
Many attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss; Lofty is Amitābha.
When sentient beings recite his name, they can extinguish the darkness of ignorance; Together they shall cross the river of suffering.
Lofty is Amitābha; his lifespan is truly difficult to surpass. With eighty-four thousand marks, Beholding him, one transcends the river of craving.
Lofty is Amitābha; many are the sentient beings who call upon him.
In an instant they ascend to the jewel realm, where their spirits are pure and forever free from demons. Victorious is Mahāsthāmaprāpta! His compassionate vows are vast and boundless.
The light from the flask atop his head shines universally, showing compassion for all his children. The ground of the Pure Land is made of lapis lazuli.
Coral and agate beads, with golden sands shining through the water;
The adorned realms are all like the land of *tathatā*—how could they not be joyful? Golden light fills every terrace;
The *maṇi* and bright moon shine, opening of their own accord when the time comes. Human life is like the morning dew; Do not linger or delay.
One must urgently and diligently recite the name, so that Amitābha may come to welcome one at that time.
Because of the cause of reciting the Buddha’s name, ignorance and delusion are extinguished. Only those who possess the profound samādhi should accord with right knowledge;
thus the Dharma-gate of Sukhāvatī is opened. That sentient beings are unwilling to come is solely because they are bound by ignorance.
For eternal kalpas they shall suffer calamity, Failing to awaken to the principle of True Suchness (Tathatā).
For a long time submerged in the river of craving, They constantly covet wealth and always lust after form; Thus they revolve through the evil realms in great numbers.

I often sigh for myself, yet rejoice that I have deeply awakened to the principle of True Suchness: Afflictions are originally non-existent; It is only through the deluded perceptions of sentient beings that they arise.
The Land of Ultimate Bliss is most subtle and profound; No one at all understands it. Within lies Amitābha as the Lord;
when performing prostrations together with him, If you wish to recognize the principle of non-arising, You need only recite the Buddha’s name.
When the clouds of worldly toil are completely dispersed, The sun of wisdom shines with brilliant clarity. If you wish to see the principle of True Suchness, [recite the Buddha’s name].

One need only contemplate the white tuft of hair; the clouds of ignorance are completely dispersed. The mirror of wisdom shines brightly, and the sublime *tathatā* (suchness) is seen through non-seeing.
This non-seeing is itself *tathatā*. If one realizes the intent within this, the Dharma-mirror reflects upon the void.
When the mind penetrates and awakens to the solidity of form, the wondrous lands of the spiritual powers appear.
The Dharma-realm is universally the same; though thoughts differ, the mind is eternally pure by nature. Divine light pervades the ten directions;
knowing the mind has no fixed location, one attains the coolness of liberation.
Contemplating forms yet seeing no forms, raising the voice yet untainted by sound— Thoroughly realizing that nothing exists, the mirror of wisdom shines with brilliant clarity.
In profound stillness, the subtle spirit is tranquil; Serene and at ease, it has no object of perception.
Seated or reclining within the celestial palace, it transcends both humans and devas. For a moment, it is drawn to stand by the pond’s edge;
It washes away the mud from within the mind, Pure and stainless, free from all defilement. I pray that you realize Bodhi, And that the mirror of wisdom never grow dim.
The wisdom-jewel is constantly used for illumination; Defilements must be severed and cast away. The precious throne naturally welcomes you;
Focus your thoughts and observe constantly. The rare and precious King of Samādhis is vast and tranquil;
Sweep away the mud within the mind through the teachings of the Tripiṭaka. If people now single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name, Those who recite shall enter deep dhyāna.
In the first watch of the night, sit with an upright mind; The Western Quarter is present before one’s eyes.
When mindfulness realizes there is no-mindfulness, that no-mindfulness is True Suchness (Tathatā). If you understand this inner meaning, It is called the Jewel of Dharmatā;
the Pure Land is within the heart. Fools seek it outwardly, Yet the precious mirror is within the heart.
Failing to realize that this one life will end, the Buddhas dwell within your own heart. You yourself are unable to seek them;
take care not to let this time pass in vain. Hasten your hands and seek with early diligence! Everyone possesses the precious mirror, yet the foolish do not know how to polish it.
Never having turned back to reflect themselves, the dust and grime only increase more and more.
If a household possesses a precious mirror, a wise person knows how to polish it; by diligently reflecting upon themselves, defilements will not intrude.
The wish-fulfilling jewel is ever luminous and clear; its self-nature is fundamentally perfect and bright.
By awakening to principle, one knows the true essence: to recite the Buddha's name is itself non-arising. Even when ground into powder, it remains a gold mine.
Gold is not seen within the ore; the wise employ smelting and refining. True gold appears within the belly as the Buddha-mark, empty and signless.
True Suchness is tranquil and speaks not; the verbal teaching of written words is the Chan of forgetting signs in this realm.
Nirvana is the final iron dharma; the secret is not transmitted through instruction.
The mind is usually used for oneself; one’s majesty should deliver those with whom one has a karmic affinity.
The Three Vehicles fundamentally do not recognize [this], and non-Buddhists have never heard of it. The minor signs have never been heard of; the vow is not to be transmitted [to the unworthy].
When meeting a worthy person on the Way, transmit it hand-in-hand. When meeting an unworthy person on the Way...
The Pure Land in the West is excellent; Every person’s path is most worthy of pity. By diligently reciting the Buddha’s name, one shall forever leave behind the realms of humans and devas.
In the Pure Land there is a golden garden; When the mind penetrates and realizes the solidity of form, Amitābha will embrace all.
May all universally vow to sit upon red lotuses, And gather from the emerald-colored lotus ponds.
Golden flowers fill every place; from jade doors, pure sounds resonate. With earnest farewells amidst the five turbidities, we shall together set our appointment for the Western Land.
Do not be deluded by the suffering of birth and death, nor harbor doubts regarding the Pure Land.
The wondrous pavilions are of purple and yellow gold; there are groves of lapis lazuli and the seven treasures. In the lotus ponds, the colors of the flowers vary in their splendor.
The Bodhisattva’s High-Flight Chant: Now I have arrived at this Pure Land; For long the lotus has stood open as my gateway.
By the power of my red vow, In a single thought, I sit upon the lotus throne.
In this pure realm, the golden trees of the altar Are draped with nets of jewels; From time to time they yield precious fruits— May all of you observe them with a sincere mind.
Jeweled palaces and golden towers, Red lotuses bloom in emerald ponds.

If one knows only to diligently recite the wondrous verses of Buddha-remembrance, The myriad phrases [of praise], Then the seven treasures shall become one’s palace, And golden lotuses shall form a dais.
Those who sincerely practice Buddha-remembrance Shall all ascend these flowers to reach The Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha.
The jewel-bird utters its song; listen to the meaning within the sound. Summoning the Dharma into the golden city, the peacock sits before the Buddha.
The mandarin ducks frolic and chant; the white cranes dance within the palace.
The myna birds play the lute of themselves; the pond waters appear before them. In the flowering grove, they accord with the Dharmakāya.
You need only uphold this wondrous scripture, which all Buddhas have realized as true. For a moment, as you sat by the side of the terrace, Amitābha beheld my body.
He asked, "O children, are you well? The person destined for rebirth was amidst a cluster of red lotuses;
furthermore, there was another cluster that was blue, and in its midst, a transformed son was born.
The words are most clear: if you wish to go to the Western Land, you need only recite the Buddha’s name and cultivate pure deeds with a resolute mind.
Lofty and sublime, you shall enter the Treasure Hall; in Sukhāvatī there are no lamps or fires, yet each form is self-illuminated.
Know only to diligently recite the Buddha’s name, and you will swiftly awaken to the non-arising of phenomena.
The World-Honored One’s supreme jeweled tower Dwells atop the City of Transformation;

May you purify your mind and strive with diligence— The Land of Ultimate Bliss will soon appear before you. If you do not see it due to ignorance, repent with all your might until your body is shattered;
Then the Compassionate Lord will come of his own accord. To the west lies the jeweled tower.
The Holy Assembly comes of its own accord; within the sound, one constantly recollects the Buddha.
In the mind, one speaks of non-arising, and the Buddhas follow the body. Those who are deluded do not exert themselves; you, O assembly, must diligently recollect.
In the heart, there is constant joy, and the wondrous land appears within the mind—all this is due to the abundance of pure karma.
With a sincere mind enter samādhi, Forever leaving behind this suffering Sahā world.
A single moment of virtuous thought in the wondrous land Is known throughout the ten directions by its name. Diligently recollect Amitābha Buddha; This is precisely the time to resolve the mind.
If you wish to seek samādhi, Nothing surpasses self-restraint of the mind. Let not body and mind be interrupted.
The Compassionate Lord came of his own accord to seek the true land of Ultimate Bliss and Purity; In other realms he had not yet found passage, so with heart and mind he sought samādhi.
Entering meditative absorption, he beheld Amitābha: The pond waters reflect golden sands, and lotus flowers grow everywhere in abundance.
Those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha shall all go there, Wandering at will as they please.
If you seek the bliss of samādhi, there is no fault greater than fragmenting the body. By truly practicing the World-Honored One’s teachings, one causes the multitude to behold the golden body;
that all Buddhas achieve the state of outflowlessness is entirely due to cultivation over successive kalpas.
Those who wish to be born in the Pure Land should diligently seek it within their own minds, amassing jewels as vast as mountain peaks.
Sentient beings are unable to seek it; Within they harbor a lamp and a mirror.

They do not know that this single life’s rest is a jeweled pavilion with golden towers and nets, Where flower rain fills the ponds and pavilions. The pure sounds of the seven-jeweled pipes do not need to be played;
they resonate spontaneously. Sustained by the Buddha’s power, Today I have emerged from the river of craving.
In an instant one is born in that land, Then returns here to save the Sahā world.
In the Pure Land, waters of golden sand constantly flow around the Buddha; If someone enters meditative concentration and sees this, With what further cause for sorrow could they rejoice?
Listen to how those born there say: "This lotus pond is my home; Riding upon the lotus, one will surely attain mastery."
Amidst the playful scattering of celestial flowers, I now abide in samādhi; The lotus-flower color glows with radiant flames as my mind dwells in the palace of the seven treasures.
Having paid homage to the Buddha, I have not yet returned; If someone were to attempt to withdraw me, the lotus petals would simply shed away.
With a refined mind, I diligently recollect the Buddha; The color of the flower grows even more radiant.
The ocean of suffering is vast and boundless; The ship of Amitābha’s vow-power Welcomes all to be born in the Pure Land, Where all shall sit upon red lotuses.
By this diligent cultivation amidst suffering, The bodhisattvas of the Pure Land Attain the highest grade among the flowers, Traveling to the ten directions in a single thought-moment.
The jeweled pavilion has no one to ascend it; hell rushes forward in competition. Once life has come to an end in a single morning, for what reason would you enter the gates of the underworld?
People of the West have reached the stronghold; hell rushes forward in competition. Recalling the Buddha is like a bright mirror;
those who commit sins remain shrouded in dark gloom. There is no need to go to hell.
Return early to the Pure Land; within its ponds lies true and wondrous bliss. For eternal kalpas, you shall no longer hear the lamentations and bitter cold of the hells.
The Ox-Headed Demon stands right before your eyes; as the sinner is about to enter, he cries out in agony and wails to heaven.
If one does not recite the Buddha’s name while alive, after death one enters the gates of the underworld.
Frequently suffering in the cauldron of boiling water, Fierce flames threaten the souls of men.
Sitting upon the throne of Śākyamuni, his disciples compete to come and listen As he describes the sufferings of this Jambudvīpa. Saṃsāra does not pause for even a moment;
The West is truly wondrous bliss, A purple lotus throne of a hundred jewels, With golden paths as its boundaries.
Those who see it will give rise to the aspiration for enlightenment; a jeweled pavilion appears in the western direction. The golden terrace is even more wondrous;
within the pond, transformed beings are born. They stir the red lotuses in the water; in the jade-green pool, the waters and lotus flowers are lush with fragrance.
When the flowers bloom, one can behold the Buddha; hearing the Dharma, one awakens to the True Constant.
The Gabled Hall is transformed into lush green; golden towers are draped with jeweled nets. Above the mani banners are canopies, and the pond waters are like a hundred flowers.

Having diligently practiced mindfulness of the Buddha throughout one’s life, with vows to leave the Sahā world uninterrupted in body and mind, one shall forever sit upon lotus blossoms, returning the mind to the mindfulness of Amitābha Buddha.
I prostrate to that Tathāgata and vow to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Sitting upon a lotus pedestal within the pond, I direct my mind toward the Western Path;
with a humble heart, I gather in all sentient beings. May Amitābha, out of his compassionate pity, see me and naturally come to welcome me when my retribution is exhausted.
Relying upon the various holy teachings, I have briefly set forth this ritual manual for the Five-Assembly Dharma Service of Praise and Eulogy.
It is considered to consist of three fascicles;
as for the first two fascicles,
their textual evidence is clearly established.
Settling the mind to dispel all doubts and turning the heart toward the Pure Land,
if you all recite, praise, and practice accordingly, [you shall attain rebirth].
This should be understood as being based on the text for the dedication of merit and the making of vows from the preceding fascicle.
It was at the beginning of winter in the tenth month of the ninth year of the Dali era.
At Longxing Temple in Beijing,
he once again expounded the contemplative gate of Pure Land recitation, so that [sentient beings] might purify their spirits and bodies and realize the perfect luminosity of wondrous enlightenment,
together dwelling in the assembly of the lotus flowers.
May all wise ones,
with deep faith, practice accordingly,
and cultivate weary detachment toward the world of saṃsāra and birth-and-death.
Exclusively reciting the name of that Buddha,
they shall go together to the Pure Land and swiftly realize Bodhi.
Is this not truly excellent and joyful?
May those who possess the karmic affinity for it together return to the West.
There are differences in the capacities of the faculties;
each follows their own karma, and that is all.

Copied in the month of Jyeṣṭhā (Rui-bin), in the year of Xinhai, when thirteen leaves of the calendrical plant had withered,
at Maitreya Hall behind the lecture hall of Daesun Soryuksa in Dangch’on.
Therefore, it is recorded.
